[page 212] එයත ගමට එනව ද? එයත ගමට එනව ද දනන න. is he coming home, too? i don't know if (whether) he is coming home, too. similarly, මහතතය වඩ කරනව ද කයනන. tell me if (whether) the master is working. තතත ගදර ද බලනන. see if (whether) father is at home. ම කම හඳ ද බලනන. see if (whether) this food is good. note that when english 'if' may be replaced by 'whether', it is ac construction in sinhalese, replaced by 'whether' it is a but when english 'if' may not be construction in sinhalese. මහතතය ගදර ඉනනව නම ඔහ මහ එනන. you come here if the master is at home. මහතතය ගදර ඉනනව ද දනන න. i don't know if (whether) the master is at home. 5. 'also whenever 'too, also is added to ee or aa, these vowels shorten to e ora in pronunciation. ಲಿಂ (eaa) 'he, she' ໙໖ (eat) 'he too, she too කඩ (kadee) 'the shop' (kadet) 'the shop, too only words of one syllable are exceptions to this rule. in these, the vowel remains long: මත (meet) 'this, too) 6. නස 'because නස 'because is used to form both phrases and clauses. 6.1 it forms phrases with a preceding noun or pronoun in the direct caве: [page 213] වරසව නස වඩ නස ඒ නස because of the rain because of the work because of that, thus 6.2 it forms clauses as follows: 1. if the sentence has a verb in the simple present form, when නස is added the verb is put in the verbal adjective form: ගනපල නයට ගනන නස මට සලල හගය. because gunapala buys on credit i am short of money. කර එක සරවස කරන නස මම බස එකන යනව. because the car is being ser-viced, i am going by bus. 2. if a sentence is a negative one with added is replaced by . when නස is ගනපල එනන නත නස සලල හඟය. because gunapala doesn't come, (i'm) short of money. වහනන නත නස අද වඩ කරනන පලවන. since it isn't raining, (we) can work today. 3. if the sentence is an equational one, or one with ໖໑, ໑໖, or කමත; නස may be added, but if the original statement had the assertion marker, this is dropped when නස is added: ම කම හඳ නස කනනම. because this food is good, i'll eat. මන හ හඳ වඩවක නස රසසවක දනන පලවන. මහතතය ඉකමනට යනන ඕන නස කර එක ඉකමනට ගනන. එයට වඩ පලවන නස රසසව දනන ඕන. මහතතය ඒකට කමත නස මම ගනනම. since he is a good carpenter (we) can give him a job. bring the car quickly, because the master wants to go right away. since he can do the work, (we) should give him the job. since the master likes that one, i'll buy (it). [page 214] 4. if the sentence is a replaces බ when නස negative one with 2 is added: බර දසතර හමබවනන බර නස ඇපතකර ලඟට යනන ඕන. because we can't see the doctor, (we) must go to the apothecary. 7. ວິທ 'scarce' the expression for 'i am short of money' is actually an equational sentence with 'scarce and 'for me added: සලල හගය. සලල සග නම මට සලල හගය. අපට සගරට හගය. some speakers of sinhalese have money is scarce. if money is scarce or if (you are) short of money. i'm short of money (literally: 'money is scarce for me'). we are short of cigarettes. rather than හග : money is scarce. සලල සඟය. 8. 'next, this, last' with expressions of time 'this, the present' and ගය means 'the coming' or 'next'; 'the past' or 'last'. ලබන මස ම මස ශය වස the coming (next) month this month the past (last) month similarly: ලබන සවන 'next week', etc. 9. genitive case quantity phrases 9.1 in lesson 8, we met quantity phrases in the genitive definite preceding nouns in expressions like 'a five-rupee ticket': [page 215] රපයල පහ තට එකක රපයල තන මදදර රපයල වසස බඩවක a five-rupee ticket three-rupee stamps a twenty-rupee piece of goods if the quantity phrase is placed in the genitive indefinite, the sense is 'tickets worth five rupees' or 'five rupees worth of tickets, etc.: රපයල පහක ටකට five rupees worth of tickets රපයල තනක මදදර three rupees worth of stamps රපයල වසසක බඩ goods worth twenty rupees 'about' may be 9.2 in either of the constructions in 9.1, used between the quantity phrase, which remains in the genitive, and the noun: රපයල වසසක බඩ goods worth twenty rupees රපයල වසසක වතර බඩ goods worth about twenty rupees රපයල පහ වතර ටකට එකක a five-rupee ticket about a five-rupee ticket 10. මක, මකක. the interrogative word sa 'what, why has the indefinite form මකක. 10.1 the definite form english 'why': is usually an equivalent for බපප ගමට ආව මකද? අද වඩ කරනන මකකද? මක and the question marker together as a single word: මකද. why did you come home, uncle? why are you working today? are frequently written [page 216] 10.2 the indefinite form a is an equivalent for english. 'what': නන ගනන මකක ද? මකක ද කරනන? what is the lady buying? what are you doing? note that මනව (lesson 2) is also 'what'. but a implies a single thing or action and මනව implies more than one: නන ගනන මනව ද? what (things) is the lady buy-ing? the definite form මක is infrequently used as an equiva-lent of 'what'. when so used it generally has the implication that one is at a loss, i.e., 'what on earth', 'what the dickens': දන කරනන මකද? what (on earth) do (we) do now? compare: දන කරනන මකක ද? what are you (we) doing now? 11. වත whenever ad is added to an interrogative word, it has a generalizing sense, like that of english 'any'. thus: මකක වත කයක වත ක දනක වත anything any number any number (of people) thus කවද වත 'any day' or 'any time is කවද 'when' plus වත. කවද වත used in negative or interrogative sentences, and then usually equates with english 'never' and 'ever' respec-tively. කවද වත නයට බඩ දනන හඳ න. it's never good to sell goods on credit. කවද වත යනන එප. don't ever go. කවද වත යනව ද? are you going any day? [page 217] 12. instrumental case the instrumental case may be used with the sense 'from' as in 'to get something from someone or somewhere: අර කඩන එලල ගනන. මහතතයගන සලල ගනන පලවන. වන හගන සලල හඟක වනන තයනවද? get vegetables from that shop. (you) can get money from the master. does he owe you much money (literally: is there much money to come from him)? note that movement from a place is generally expressed by the ඉඳල construction that you have been using since lesson 1; and not by the instrumental case: මහ ඉඳල බස එකන යනන. go by bus from here: 13. 'it's raining' 'it's raining' is expressed in sinhalese by the verb without a subject. dative case: the place where it is raining is in the දන එහට වහනව. ම දවස වල ඒ පතතට වහනව. it's raining there now. these days it is raining in that area. 14. numerals 13 20 the inanimate numeral දහන ව is a class 4 noun. other inanimate numerals from 'thirteen' to 'twenty belong to class 2. inanimate genitive stem දහතන thirteen දහතන දහ තන දහතර fourteen දහතර දහතර පලස, පහලස පලභ, පහලහ fifteen පලහ, පහලහ sixteen දහසය දහ සය ද හත seventeen ද හත ද හත දහ අට eighteen දහ අට දහ අට [page 218] දහන ම nineteen twenty genitive දහන ම stem දහ නම อล the animate forms are, as usual, made by adding the stem: දන to දහතන දන thirteen දහත දන seventeen දහතර දන fourteen දහ අට දන eighteen පලස දන fifteen දහනම දන nineteen or පහලස දන වස දන twenty දහසය දන sixteen exercises a. substitute orally: 1. 2. දනන න. if gunapala is coming home if mr. perera is in the estate if he is a good doctor if there is work in the estate if it is raining there now if the lady is in that same estate if this food is good if the (paternal) uncle came home if father is short of money these days if gunapala can do carpentry මහතතය ගදර ද see tell me i don't know do (you) know? can (you) tell me? PERERA ආයි බෝ hello ආයිබෝ! එන්න, එන්න. Hello. Come. Come වාඩිවෙන්න. Sit down. සැප සනීප comfort and health කොහොම ද සැප සනීප? How are you? MR. GUNASEKERA වරද the fault වරදක් නෑ. Not too bad. GUNASEKERA the baby, child Where are the children? PERERA both Both are at school. the shop And (my) wife went shopping. GUNASEKERA Isn't it vacation yet? PERERA They haven't given vacation in the school over here yet. the end Vacation will be given at the end of the month. news What news of your area? GUNASEKERA new There's nothing new. the house make [page 224] අපි අලුත් ගෙයක් හැදුවා. We built a new house. GUNASEKERA move into a new house No. We will move in next month. That's what I came to say. the third (day) Third of next month. everybody All of you must come. PERERA Yes. I'll bring you something to drink. What will you have? tea coffee Tea or coffee? GUNASEKERA කරදරේ කරදර වෙන්න එපා. the trouble No. Don't bother. GUNASEKERA තේ එකක් හොඳයි. No. A cup of tea will be fine. PERERA දානවා milk put කිරි දානවා ද? You take milk? GUNASEKERA කිරි එපා. No. No milk. PERERA සීනි? sugar Sugar? ' so how? is an expression that can be used in response to the first participant as illustrated in the con-versation above. කහම ද expressions are used by friends only. 3.2 other idioms the following idioms are not restricted to the type of conver-sation discussed above. ඒක නං. that's certain. වරදක න. not too bad. 4. linking- the linking-which has been learned with the meaning 'too' (14.3) may also be used as an equivalent of the english 'and' in connecting one statement with a preceding one. බබල ඉසකල. නනත සපප ගය. the children are at school. and my wife went shopping. 5. ordinal numerals the ordinals for the first twenty numerals are the following: පලවන දවන තනවන හතරවන හය වන හතවන first second third fourth fifth sixth seventh eighth නමවන ninth දහවන tenth එකලසවන eleventh දලසවන twelfth පසවන දහතනවන thirteenth දහතරවන fourteenth පලසවන fifteenth අටවන දහසයවන sixteenth [page 229] දහතවන දහ අටවන seventeenth eighteenth දහනම වන වසවන nineteenth twentieth note that in all cases except for 'first' and 'second' the form -වන is added to the same numeral stem that is used in mak-ing animate numerals (10, 6.2) 5.1 ordinal numerals may be used with either animate or inani-mate nouns with no change in form: තනවන පනතය තනවන මහතතය the third grade the third gentleman 5.2 note that the form may be added to all these ordinals to express dates: තනවනද අටවනද ඉරද the third day the eighth day which occurs at the end of the names for the this is the same days of the week: e.g.: අඟහරවද sunday monday tuesday, etc. 6. everybody' the word කවරත 'everybody' refers to people only, whereas සරම 'everybody', 'everything', 'all' may refer to people සරම හනදය තයනව. or things: කවරත එනන ඕන. everybody must come. සරම ගමට ගය. everybody went home. everything is at the corner. 7. ٠٠٠ in questions involving an alternative, sinhalese uses.. ٠٠٠ where english uses 'or'. මනව ද හඳ? තද? කප ද? මහතතය යනන කලඹට ද? what is good? tea or coffee? is the master going to colombo කලතරට ද? or to kalutara? [page 230] 8. when is added to the definite form of the numeral 'two' (either animate 6 or inanimate දක ) it equates with english 'both'. when added to the definite form of other numerals it equates with english 'all' as in: තනදන ම තන ව all three (persons) all three (things) thus: දනන ම ඉසකල. both are at school. 9. පසස the postposition පසස may equate with english 'after', con-trasting with g ໖໖ó 'before' (14,9). like ดู໖໖ it may be used with the dependent noun in the dative case. මම හයට පසස එනනම. මම හයට ඉසසර එනනම. මහතතය ඊට ඉසසර කලඹට යව. i'll come after six o'clock. i'll come before six o'clock. the master might go to colombo before that. මහතතය ඊට පසස කලඹට යව. the master might go to colombo after that. may also equate with english 'in' stating a period of time. this usage meaning 'before the end of a period of the postposition meaning 'at the end of', contrasts with ඉසසර time': මසකට පසස කලඹට යනනම . සමනකට ඉසසර ආපහ එනන. i'll go to colombo after a month. come back before the end of the week. the expression හඟක කලකට පසස, නද ? i haven't seen you for a long time is literally 'after a long time'. [page 231] 10. ත එක ත 'tea', බර 'beer', 'coffee and other names of beverages may be used in quantity phrases with the numeral 'one' or other numerals implying "so many glasses or cups," just as english may say 'a beer, two coffees, etc.': ත එකක හදනනම. බර දකක ගනන. i'll make a (cup of) tea. bring two beers. 11. ත එකක බනව ද? when in offering somebody something in english it is customary to say 'do you want such and such'; in sinhalese in a similar but rather the verb situation it is not customary to use which is proper to that situation: ත එකක බනව ද? බර එකක බනව ද? do you want a cup of tea? do you want a beer? another way of offering somebody something in sinhalese is to use the- form of the verb: කප එකක බම. let's have a cup of coffee. this is a more friendly expression. 12. some sinhalese sentence constructions a summary some sinhalese sentence constructions are different from their english equivalents in that they (1) are formed with words like පලවන ඕන or කමත rather than verbs, or (2) involve special cases of subjects and objects. those that have been met so far are summarized in the following sentences. two new points are illustrated by the negative emphatic sentences: (1) 2 appears as බර (13,4) in emphatic sentences, and (2) ໑ has an emphatic form නතත not been met before. the latter form has 12.1 පලවන and constructions: 1. with dative case subjects: [page 232] simple sentences: positive negative මට සංහල පලවන. i can (speak) sinhalese. මට සංහල බ. i can't (speak) sinhalese. මට පත ඕන. i want books. මට පත එප/ඕන න. i don't want books. මට යනන පලවන. i can go. මට යනන බ. i can't go. වට යනන ඕන. i want to go. මට යනන ඕන න. i don't want to go. emphatic sentences: මට පලවන සංහල. it is sinhalese that i can (speak). මට බර සංහල it is sinhalese that i can't (speak). මට ඕන පත. it is books that i want. මට එප පත. it is books that i don't want. or මට ඕන නතත පත. it is books that i don't want. මට පලවන යනන. what i can do is go. මට බර යනන. what i can't do is go. මට ඕන යනන. what i want to do is go. මට ඕන නතත යනන. what i don't want to do is go. [page 233] 2. with direct case subjects: simple sentences: positive ටම යනන ඕන. i must go. emphatic sentences: යනන ඕන මට. it is i who must go. negative මම යනන ඕන න. i needn't go. යනන ඕන නතත මම. it is i who needn't go. 12.2 කමත constructions simple sentences: positive මම පතට කමතය. i like the book. මට යනන කමතය. i like to go. emphatic sentences: මම කමත පතට. it is the book that i like. මම කමත යනන. what i like to do is go. negative මම පතට කමත න. i don't like the book. මම යනන කමත න. i don't like to go. මම කමත නතත පතට. what i don't like is the book. මම කමත නතත යනන. what i don't like to do is go. 12.3 ඉනනව and තයනව constructions 1. with dative case subjects: simple sentences: positive මට පතක ඉනනව. i have a son. පට පතක තයනව. i have a book negative මට පතක න. i don't have a son. මට පතක . i don't have a book. [page 234] emphatic sentences: positive මට ඉනන පතක. it is a son that i have. මට තයනන පතක. it is a book that i have. negative මට නතත පතක. it is a son that i don't have. මට නතත පතක. it is a book that i don't have. 2. with direct case subjects: simple sentences: positive ලටය ගදර ඉනනව. the child is home. පත චතන තයනව. the book is here. emphatic sentences: ලමය ඉනන ගදර. the child is home. පත තයනන මතන. the book is here. negative ලමය ගදර න. the child isn't home. පත මතන න. the book isn't here. ලමය නතත ගදර. where the child isn't, is home. පත නතත මතන. where the book isn't, is here. exercises a. substitute orally: 1. මක second sixth first පනතය පතක ද? fourth third twelfth [page 235] [page 236] [page 237] [page 238] [page 239] [page 240] [page 241] [page 242]

PAST TENSE Those Verbs can be divided into three regular classes depending on the formation of the past tense. These classes may be recognized on the basis of the last vowel in the present tense stem. verbs with a stem ending in a or a will be called Class 1 those with a stem ending in I, Class 2, and those with a stem ending in -e, Class 3. There is a change in the stem of the past by comparison with the present stem that applies to all the regular classes. If certain vowels occur in non-final position in the present stem, then these are replaced by other vowels in the past stem for all three classes, as follows: In the present stem: a Replacement in the past stem: is replaced by is replaced by e is replaced by e u is replaced by 1 If the vowel of the present stem is long, the vowel of the past stem will be the same replacement as above, but also long. Any other vowel that occurs in the present stem will remain in the past stem. 3.1 Class 1 Class 1 verbs are characterized by their stems ending in vowel -a, or in a if h precedes: wahanewa 'close'. Besides the vowel replacement mentioned above, Class 1 verbs change the final e to -uw to form the past stem. Thus the present stem ৯৫- (bale-) has the past stem - (bæluw-). To this past stem a is added [page 249] to form the simple past and e to form the emphatic past. Thus, බැලුවා, බැලුවෙ Those verbs which end in-yə or we, such as කියනවා, කියවනවා are an exception. They change ya or we to -ww-. Thus, present stem 23- (kiya), past stem present stem 30- (kiyəwə-); past stem ໖໖໖ -(kiyeww-). 'be supposed to', 'have to' the construction with a and the subject in the dative 'be supposed to with an infinitive case has already been learned. මට යනන තයනව. i am supposed to go. the past of this is formed with the past of ຜທ : මට යනන නඋන i was supposed to go. a similar construction occurs with the verb ເປັພ 'to become'. with the form as the implication is future, 'i will have to' and with the form 3 the implication is past, 'i had to' or 'it became necessary for me to. මට පයන යනන උන. මහතතය එනව නම මට වඩ කරනන වනව. i had to go on foot. if the boss comes, i'll have to work. 9. නම 9.1 when occurs as a conjunction 'if' at the end of a clause with a present tense verb (12,5), the implication may be either present or future, and the verb of the other ("then") clause will be in the form demanded by the sense: [page 264] මහතතය කලතරට යනව නම, මත යනනම. මහතතය ඉනන ගදර නම, මම ටලපන කරනනම. if the master is going to kalutara, i'll go too. if the master is at home, i'll telephone him. when the verb of a නම 'if clause is in the simple past tense, the implication is generally past contrary to fact (if he .'). the verb of the other clause will commonly had gone be in the present tense: තව ටකක පරකක උන නම, මහතතය අලල ගනන හමබ වනන න. එය කනතරවට ගය නම, ලක මහතතය හමබ වනව. if i had been a bit later, i wouldn't have been able to catch him. if he had gone to the office, he would have met the big boss. 9.2 besides meaning 'if', may sometimes be an equivalent of english 'of course'. in this usage it does not follow a clause but occurs immediately following the item that 'of course applies to: එහ වනද නම කර එකක සයගනන beයනව. මම නම යනන ඕන. other days, of course, a car is available there. i, of course, must go. (if i must go, you stay.) 10. bයනව, ඉනනව it has been noted (chapter 6, 3) that serves as the negative of තයනව and ඉනනව මහතතය ගදර ඉනනව. පත ගදර තයනව. මහතතය ගදර න. පත ගදර න. the master is at home the book is at home. the master is not at home. the book is not at home. in the past tense the negative is a 2 and උනන න මහතතය ගදර උනන. the master was at home. පත ගදර ත උන. the book was at home. [page 265] මහනතය ගදර උනන න. පත ගදර තඋන න. the master wasn't at home. the book wasn't at home. 11. හමබ වනව the verb ໙໖໖ ໑໙໖ besides having the meaning 'meet' may have the meaning 'to have a chance to', 'to have an opportunity to when used with a dependent infinitive. in this construction the subject is in the dative case: මහ මට සංහල කත කරනන හමබ වනව. මහ මට සංහල කත කරනන හමබ මට මහනතය අලල ගනන හමබ උන න. here i get the chance to speak sinhalese. here i don't get a chance to speak sinhalese. i didn't get the chance to catch the gentleman. 12. 'it seems' the form the end of any clause dependent upon it. when added to has the meaning 'it seems that' and is added at @they take the form and බර respectively. 2002 and මහතතය ගදර. මහතතය ගදර c. ලමය කඩ උනන. ලමය කඩ උනන . ලමයට යනන ලමයට යනන බර ල. the master is home. it seems that the master is home. the boy was in the shop. it seems that the boy was in the shop. the boy can't go. it seems that the boy can't go. 13. වනව the verb s may have the meaning 'to happen'. in this usage 'what' is usually expressed by මකද වනන? මකද උන? what's happening? what happened? 14. ໖໖ [page 266] อ໖ is a form used to intensify the item immediately preceding it and is thus likely to be the equivalent of english 'at least', 'even': හට වත ලක මහතතය හමබ වනන පලවන වවද? මට වත හමබ උන න. පතට වත පත න. will it be possible to see the big boss at least tomorrow? even i didn't get (it). even the son doesn't have books. 15.08 the form 3 is used in combination with interrogatives to form an indefinite: කහම හර එනන. මම කහ හර යනන ඕන. come somehow or other. i must go somewhere or other. exercises a. substitute orally: 1. මට බස එකක ගනන couldn't became possible wanted got fed up want can't can won't be necessary didn't become necessary don't get fed up might become impossible might be necessary don't want didn't get fed up didn't become impossible 2. ම මහතතයට doesn't understand doesn't understand enough didn't understand enough hasn't enough time didn't have enough time became late hasn't enough books [page 267] [page 268] [page 269]

text: Lesson 19 Lesson 19 [page 270] Conversation: Visiting Ceylon John is introduced to the headmaster of a village school in Ceylon by his friend Silva. JOHN the truth That's true. India between the difference We too find it difficult to tell the difference between the Ceylonese and Indians. HEADMASTER පිටසර ගැන සුමානයක් හමාරක් මහත්වයාට පිටසර පිවිතේ ගැන දැනගන්න ඕන නම් සුමානයක් හමාරක් මෙහේ නවතින්න එන්න. කෑම් බීම් නම් මහත්මයාට පුරුදු කැම බීම් නම් මෙහේ countryside, rural area the life about a week or so If you want to know (something) about the country life come to stay here for a week or so. accustomed foods and drinks of course We don't have the foods and drinks you are used to, of course. [page 274] නමුත් ඉගනගන්න බොහොම දේවල් තියෙනවා. But there are many things to learn. PLURAL NOUN INFLECTION 15.1 Classes 1-4 The direct plural form, as discussed earlier, is not predictable from the singular. The other plural case forms have an oblique stem formed by the addition of the suffix -- to the direct form. (The term oblique includes all the case forms except the direct form). PAST CONDITIONAL this much that much that much that much The past conditional form is formed from the simple past form of the verb by replacing the final a or aa by -ot: [page 296] Simple Present Simple Past Conditional එනවා come ආවා ආවොත් යනවා go ගියා ගියොත් වෙනවා become උනා උනෝත් බලනවා see, look බැලුවා බැලුවොත් This verb form is used in the 'if' clause of a conditional sen-tence. This construction implies that the action of the conditi-onal form should precede in time the action of the main verb of the sentence. It is likely to imply a future condition. Note that in the Sinhalese sentence only the form of the verb signals English 'if'. In the main clause the verb form is any reasonable form to fit the situation: මහත්තයා ආවොත් ඔහේ කොළඹ යන්න. PAST PARTICIPLE The past participle form of a verb is formed as follows: Class 1 Class 1 verbs add to the verb stem. Simple Present Past Participle බලනවා look බලලා කපනවා cut do කපලා කරලා කරනවා [page 297] An alternative form of the past participle for Class 1 verbs adds to the stem before adding: Simple Present බලනවා කපනවා නවත්තනවා look cut stop (transitive) Past Participle බලාලා කපාලා නවත්තාලා This alternative form is used widely in some dialects of Sinhalese, so the student should be prepared to meet it. Both forms are acceptable Sinhalese. Class 2 Class 2 verbs change the stem vowel a to æ, u to 1, o to e; replace the final vowel -1 of the stem by a and add . Simple Present Past Participle බඳිනවා tie බැඳලා අදිනවා draw Class 3 Class 3 verbs replace the final e of the stem by -1 and add වැටෙනවා තේරෙනවා fall understand වැටලා An alternative form of the past participle for Class 3 verbs has a long -11 instead of the short -1 if the stem is two sylla-bles and the first syllable is not long. Thus: වැටෙනවා තේරෙනවා වැටීලා, වැටලා but only e The people who use this version of the Class 3 past participle are those who use the alternative version of Class 1. 'GLAD, PLEASED' 8.1 Expressions such as a 'glad' or 'pleased' and 'glad', 'like' may be used with a dependent noun or pronoun in the dative case: මම නැටුම් වලට කැමතියි. මම ඒකට සන්තෝසයි. I like dances. I am pleased about it. 8.2 The same forms may be used with a dependent infinitive equivalent to English 'glad to', 'pleased to', although this construction may only be used if the subject of ຜຜ or ໑໖ is identical with the subject of the infinitive. මම ඒ පලාතට යන්න කැමතියි. I like to go to that area. In this construction, the student is advised to use only, because ຜ is more rarely used. 8.3 Likewise, the same expressions may take a simple present or simple past tense in the dative case (i.e., with added to the simple present or past). In this usage the subject of or සන්තොස may or may not be the same as the subject of the dependent verb. If they are the same, the construction may [page 300] equate with the English 'glad to', 'pleased to', or 'glad that', 'pleased that', and is an alternative to the construction with an infinitive. In this construction, the student is advised to use only සන්තෝස since කැමති 1s more rarely used. If the subject of ຜ or ໑໖ is different from the subject of the dependent verb, then the construction will equate with English 'glad that', 'pleased that' and in this case only this construction and not the one with the infinitive is used: මම මහත්තයා හම්බ උනාට සන්තෝසයි. 'glad, pleased' 8.1 expressions such as a 'glad' or 'pleased' and 'glad', 'like' may be used with a dependent noun or pronoun in the dative case: මම නටම වලට කමතය. මම ඒකට සනතසය. i like dances. i am pleased about it. 8.2 the same forms may be used with a dependent infinitive equivalent to english 'glad to', 'pleased to', although this construction may only be used if the subject of ຜຜ or ໑໖ is identical with the subject of the infinitive. මම ඒ පලතට යනන කමතය. i like to go to that area. in this construction, the student is advised to use only, because ຜ is more rarely used. 8.3 likewise, the same expressions may take a simple present or simple past tense in the dative case (i.e., with added to the simple present or past). in this usage the subject of or සනතස may or may not be the same as the subject of the dependent verb. if they are the same, the construction may [page 300] equate with the english 'glad to', 'pleased to', or 'glad that', 'pleased that', and is an alternative to the construction with an infinitive. in this construction, the student is advised to use only සනතස since කමත 1s more rarely used. if the subject of ຜ or ໑໖ is different from the subject of the dependent verb, then the construction will equate with english 'glad that', 'pleased that' and in this case only this construction and not the one with the infinitive is used: මම මහතතය හමබ උනට සනතසය. i'm glad to have met you. or i'm glad that i met you. මම මහතතය එනවට කමතය. i'm glad that you are coming. 9. බලනව try' බලනව 'to see when used with a dependent infinitive has the meaning 'to try'. මම හට එනන බලනනම. i'll try to come tomorrow. ම වඩ අද ඉවර කරනන බලනන. try to finish this work today. 10. ඉසසලල the form ໖ 'before' is used with a dependent noun in the dative case (like ໑໖໖໒--14,9) or with a dependent verb in the infinitive. කමට ඉසසලල බර එකක බමද? shall we have a beer before eating? එනන ඉසසලල ලයමක දනන. write to me before coming. 11. වඩය ໖໖ used with most adjectives equates with the english com-parative, i.e., වඩය හඳ 'is better than', වඩය අමර 'more difficult than', as stated in 19, 7.3. when used with the adjective ໙໖ 'different this combination equates with english 'different from'. [page 301] මහතතය ලමයට වඩය හඳය. ම එලල අර එලල වලට වඩය හඳ ද? පත මට වඩය වනස. the master is better than the boy. are those vegetables better than those? the son is different from me. 12. ඇත 12.1 the form 48 'might be', 'must be may be used with adjectives: මක හඳ ඇත. ම වඩ අමර ඇත. this might be good. this work must be difficult. 12.24 may also be added to a sentence with the verb in the simple present form: මහතතය දකන පලත වඩ කරනව ඇත. the master must be working in the southern province. මරකරය අද ඉකමනට එනව ඇත. the watchman might be coming early today. 13. නවඩව note that the direct plural form & may be used as an adjec-tive, as in the expression ඉසකල නවඩ කලක lat a time the school is on vacation'. exercises a. substitute orally: 1. as much as in our village බඩ න. as much as in the shop as much as in the south as much as in colombo as much as in the north as much as there as much as in the west as much as in my house as much as in our school area as much as in the eastern province [page 302] [page 303] [page 304] [page 305] [page 306] [page 307] [page 308] [page 309] [page 310] [page 311]

THE PAST TEMPORAL GERUND The past temporal gerund is formed from the simple past tense form of the verb by adding Thus: Simple Past Past Temporal Gerund පටන් ගත්තා started පටන් ගත්තාම ගියා went ගියාම කැපුවා cut කැපුවාම FLEC drew ඇද්දාම වැටුනා fell වැටුනාම Note that the vowel before me is always pronounced as long aa, whether the final vowel of the simple past is long or short: giyaa, giyaame, kapuwa, kapuwaame. This form is used to introduce a subordinate temporal clause the time of which is previous to the time of the main clause. Its use parallels that of the present temopral gerund which in-troduces a subordinate clause, the time of which is either contemporaneous with or future to the time of the main clause. Thus: [page 326] මහත්තයා එනකොට මම වැඩ කරන්නම්. I'll work when (at the time) the master comes (or I'll be working when he comes). මහත්තයා ආවාම මම වැඩ කරන්නම්. I'll work when (after) the master comes. වැඩ පටන් ගන්න කොට ගුනපාල ගියා. වැඩ පටන්ගත්තාම ගුනපාල ගියා. Gunapala went away when (at the time) the work was start-ing. Gunapala went away when (after) the work started. Both these gerunds are likely to equate with an English 'when' clause. 17. FOUR OR FIVE' The Sinhalese equivalent 'three or four'. With other verbs, 'might' is expressed by adding 4 simple present form: to the මහත්තයා හෙට ඒ කාර් එක ගන්නවා ඇති. The master might buy that car tomorrow. උන්නැහේ හෙට කන්තෝරුවෙ නවතිනවා ඇති. PAST PARTICIPLES 3.1 Complex Verbs The past participle may occur immediately preceding another verb to form a COMPLEX VERB. Complex verbs commonly take on special meanings, and one formed with a past participle plus a form of ໑໙໖, 'give' frequently has the meaning 'perform the action of the past participle for someone else'. Thus e 'make something for someone else'. The person for whom the action is performed, if expressed, is in the dative. The whole complex verb acts as a single verb, with a in whatever form the sentence requires. මම කරියක් හදලා දෙන්නම්. ඔහේ මහත්තයාට වැටක් බැඳලා දුන්නා ද? මට ඔහේට හොඳ මස් කරියක් හදලා දෙන්න පුලුවනි. 3.2 Manner of an Action I'll make (you) a curry. Did you build the fence for the master? I can make you a good meat curry. Sometimes the past participle of a verb occurring in a sentence or clause with a main verb may indicate the manner in which the action of the main verb is performed. මස් එපා නම් ඉස්සො දාලා හදන්න පුලුවනි. If you don't want meat, I can make it with (literally: [page 341] මිරිස් අඩු කරලා හදන්න ද? 'having put) shrimp. Should I make it reducing the pepper? The main verb and the past participle may each have its own objects and modifiers, but the subject of both must be the same. ඉස්සො දාලා කරියක් හදන්න. PARTICIPIAL SENTENCES 4.1 A past participle without another verb may form the predicate of a sentence. The implication is generally that the action has been completed, so that the usual English equivalent is the per-fect (1.e., 'has gone'): මහත්තයා ගිහිල්ලා. එලෝලුයි මසුයි බත් එක්ක කලවම් කරලා දුන්නෙලෙන් බැදලා. The master has (or 'is') gone. Vegetables and meat mixed to-gether with rice have been fried in duntel. In this usage, the subject of the participial sentence will be in the third person. Where this completive sense is required with the first person, the simple past is used: මම ඒ වැඩ කෙරුවා. I did that work. [page 342] 4.2 With a ๑๑ 'when' clause expressed or implied, a past participial sentence implies an action completed prior to that of the Goo clause, and thus equates with an English pluperfect (1.e., 'had gone'). In this usage, the subject may be any per-son, first, second, or third: ඔහේ එන කොට මම කොලඹ ගිහිල්ලා. When you came, I had gone to Colombo. 4.3 Participial vs. Perfect Sentences 4.31 The Sinhalese present perfect (21,5) may have a completive sense like that of the past participle given in 4.1 implying that the action has been completed in the recent past: මහත්තයා ගිහිල්ලා තියෙනවා. The master has gone. බංඩා පොල් ටිකක් කඩලා තියෙනවා. Banda has picked some coconuts. In this sense, the subject will be third person, as with the participle alone. 4.32 The present perfect may indicate that one has had the experience of doing something at usage, the subject may be first, some time in the past. In this second, or third person: මට කොළඹ ශිහිල්ලා තියෙනවා. I have gone to Colombo (I've been there). බංඩා පොල් කඩලා තියෙනවා. Banda has picked coconuts (he has had the experience). Sentences with the particple alone are not used in this sense. 5. One use is in repeating what someone else has said. Here it is used along with ຜາ and follows the repeated statement: නෝනා මට සල්ලි දුන්නා කියලා කිව්වා. The lady said (she) gave me the money. Another use of a is in indicating the name of something. Here again it is used with the verb Bua, and the name of the thing in question precedes ඒකට කියන්නෙ සීගිරි ගල කියලා. That is called 'Sigiriya Rock'. හුඟක් දෙනා මේ බත් වලට කියන්නෙ ප්‍රයිඩ් රයිස් කියලා. Many people call that 'fried rice.' [page 345] In these sentences it is permissible to leave out w although it is more customary to use it: නෝනා මට සල්ලි දුන්නා කිව්වා. ඒකට කියන්නෙ සීගිරි ගල. හුඟක් දෙනා මේ බත් වලට කියන්නේ ප්‍රයිඩ් රයිස්. 7. වැඩි and වැඩි 'too much', and a 'not enough' (10,8) are used in a number of ways, with English equivalents depending on their use. Both may occur with or without the assertion marker when final in simple sentences. 7.1 In constructions with a or as either meaning 'there is, there are' or 'have', ໖໖ and 3 may replace &ຜາ , ຫາ meaning 'there are too many, I have too many' or 'there aren't enough, I haven't enough', respectively: මෙහේ එලොලු වැඩියි. There are too many vegetables here. මෙහේ එලෝලු මදියි. There aren't enough vegetables here. වට සල්ලි වැඩියි. I have too much money. මට සල්ලි මදියි. I haven't enough money. 7.2 These forms may be used with other verbs in the meaning 'too much', 'not enough': මහත්තයා වැඩ කරනවා මදියි. The master doesn't work enough. මහත්තයා වැඩ කරනවා වැඩියි. The master works too much. 7.3 Following adjectives, they mean 'too .' or 'not enough': මේ ‍ගේ ලොකු මදියි. මේ ගේ ලොකු වැඩියි. ලොකු වැඩි ගෙවල් හොඳ නෑ. ලොකු මදී ගෙවල් කඩන්න. This house isn't big enough. This house is too big. Too large houses aren't good. Demolish the houses that are not big enough. [page 346] 7.4 Used as adjectives preceding nouns, the mean 'the extra or excess amount', 'the number, amount that is lacking': වැඩි පොල් අත්තෙන්ට දාන්න. මදී පොල් ගේන්න යන්න. Put the extra coconuts there. Go get the (number of) coconuts that are lacking. 8. වැඩියෙ ra, in addition to having the meaning 'more than' (19,8), has the meaning 'much' when used in negative sentences: මම සිංහල කෑම වැඩියෙ කන්නේ නෑ. මම මේ කෑම ජාති ගැන වැඩියෙ දන්නෙ නෑ. මහත්තයා වැඩියෙ ගෙදර නැ. I don't eat much Sinhalese food. I don't know much about these kinds of food. The master isn't at home much. 9. ගැන ගැන 'about, concerning takes a dependent noun in the direct case: වඩු වැඩ ගැන මොකුත් දන්නේ නෑ. I don't know anything about carpentry. ලමයා ගැන මොකද කරන්නෙ? What are you going to do about the boy? 10. 'IN SINHALESE' 'In a language' is expressed with the instrumental case of the language name: සිංහලෙන් නමක් නැ, මහත්තයා . ඒකට සිංහලෙන් කියන්නෙ මොකක්ද? මේකට සිංහලෙන් කියන්නෙ මොකක් ද? There isn't a name (for that) in Sinhalese, sir. What is that called in Sinhalese? What is this called in Sinhalese? [page 347] Note that in the sentences above the word for 'this, that' is in the dative case. 11. 'WHAT DOES IT MEAN?' The common Sinhalese expression for 'what does it mean' is තියන්නෙ මොකක් ද? or කියන්නෙ මොනවා ද , preceded by the (Sinhalese) word or phrase for which the meaning is being asked. may always be used in such a construction, but the singular: මොනවා ද only in ප්‍රයිඩ් රයිස් කියන්නෙ මොනවා ද? What does 'pol geDiyə mean? 12. ...08... හරි. . 8 is a conjunction with the English equivalent 'either. or'. 8 follows each of the two or more items listed: එලෝලු හරි මස් හරි ගේන්න. Don't you have chicken or beef? 13. A PORTION With names of foods, as with drinks (16, 11), quantity expres-sions occur implying portions or servings of the food. These follow the normal quantity phrase construction, that is, the noun is plural and the forms ໑໑, ໑໙, etc., are used: [page 348] එලෝලු දෙක බත් දෙකක් කරි තුන the two (servings of) vegetables two (servings of) rice the three portions of curry Parallel to these constructions the form on may be used with the plural form of the name of a food, implying a single portion or serving: එලෝලු එක the serving of vegetables බත් එකක් a portion of rice කෑම එකක් a meal කරි එක the portion of curry 14. THE PLURALS OF THE A SET The plurals of මේක 'this one', අරක, ඕක, ඒක that one', are these', 46, ໖໖, 'those'. 'four or five', etc., may be expressed without a conjunction. if the form required is an indefinite, both numerals will be indefinite for inanimate expressions, but for animates only the last one will be indef1-nite, and the first one will be the stem form: මට රපයල දකක තනක දනන. give me two or three rupees. මහ මනසස තන හතර දනක ඉනනව. here there are three or four people. when the intensive particle is added to such an expression, the meaning is 'as much as', 'as many as': මට පත හතරක පහක ම තයනව. i have (as many as) four or five books. මට ලමය දතන දනක ම ඉනනව. i have (as many as) two or three boys. 18. instrumental case when something is given, dispersed or distributed to people generally by an organization or institution, the organization or institution is in the instrumental case: [page 327] වයදම කරනන ආංඩවන. the government incurs the expenses. ම පර අඩවන හදනව. this road the government builds. 19. banda has picked coconuts (he has had the experience). sentences with the particple alone are not used in this sense. 5. the past participial adjective 5.1 the regular past participial adjective is formed as follows: for the first two classes of verbs the of the past par-ticiple is replaced by -g note that there are alternative forms corresponding to those of the past participle: [page 343] present simple past participle past participial adjective class 1: bot boll (solids) තමබනව තමබල, තමබල තමබප, තමබප look, see බලනව බලල, බලල බලප, බලප class 2: fry බදනව බදල බදප fetch, අදනව draw for verbs of class 3, is replaced by -verbs there are no alternative forms of the past participial adjective, even if there are for the past participle. only the for class 3 form with (short) -1- occurs in the adjective: present simple past participle past participial adjective fall වටනව වටල, වටල වටචච understand තරනව the verbs with irregular past participial adjectives that have occurred so far are: present simple past participle past participial adjective come එනව ඇවලල, ඇවත 429 take away ගනයනව ගනහලල, ගනහන ගනයප take ගනනව අරගන, අරන අරගතත bring ගනව ගනලල ගනප burn දනව බල ප go දව drink බනව ගහලල ගයප be (1nan.) තල යනව දල දප give දනව වල වචච move in become ගවදනව ගවදල ගවදචච put, place දනව දල 9ay eat කනව පනව කල කප be seen පනල පනචච [page 344] 5.2 the past participial adjective modifies following nouns. the meaning may be either that whatever is expressed by the noun has performed the action or that the action has been performed upon it, depending upon context. the most common english equivalent is a relative clause, usually with a verb in the perfect, modify-ing a noun. in the following pairs, the first sentence of each is a sentence formed with a past participle and the second con-tains a noun modified by a past participial adjective: බංඩ පල කඩල. බංඩ කඩප පල අදනන. ම කම තලන බදල. තලන බදප බත බර වඩය, නද? පල වටල. වටචච පල මතනට දනන. banda has picked coconuts. fetch the coconuts that banda has picked. this food has been fried in oil. food fried in oil is too heavy, isn't it? the coconuts have fallen. put the fallen coconuts (or 'the coconuts that have fallen') here. 6. කයල ຜ the past participle of ຜຫາ 'tell, call', has some special uses not shared by other past participles. one use is in repeating what someone else has said. here it is used along with ຜາ and follows the repeated statement: නන මට සලල දනන කයල කවව. the lady said (she) gave me the money. another use of a is in indicating the name of something. here again it is used with the verb bua, and the name of the thing in question precedes ඒකට කයනන සගර ගල කයල. that is called 'sigiriya rock'. හඟක දන ම බත වලට කයනන ප‍රයඩ රයස කයල. many people call that 'fried rice.' [page 345] in these sentences it is permissible to leave out w although it is more customary to use it: නන මට සලල දනන කවව. ඒකට කයනන සගර ගල. හඟක දන ම බත වලට කයනන ප‍රයඩ රයස. 7. වඩ and වඩ 'too much', and a 'not enough' (10,8) are used in a number of ways, with english equivalents depending on their use. both may occur with or without the assertion marker when final in simple sentences. 7.1 in constructions with a or as either meaning 'there is, there are' or 'have', ໖໖ and 3 may replace &ຜາ , ຫາ meaning 'there are too many, i have too many' or 'there aren't enough, i haven't enough', respectively: මහ එලල වඩය. there are too many vegetables here. මහ එලල මදය. there aren't enough vegetables here. වට සලල වඩය. i have too much money. මට සලල මදය. i haven't enough money. 7.2 these forms may be used with other verbs in the meaning 'too much', 'not enough': මහතතය වඩ කරනව මදය. the master doesn't work enough. මහතතය වඩ කරනව වඩය. the master works too much. 7.3 following adjectives, they mean 'too .' or 'not enough': ම ‍ග ලක මදය. ම ග ලක වඩය. ලක වඩ ගවල හඳ න. ලක මද ගවල කඩනන. this house isn't big enough. this house is too big. too large houses aren't good. demolish the houses that are not big enough. [page 346] 7.4 used as adjectives preceding nouns, the mean 'the extra or excess amount', 'the number, amount that is lacking': වඩ පල අතතනට දනන. මද පල ගනන යනන. put the extra coconuts there. go get the (number of) coconuts that are lacking. 8. වඩය ra, in addition to having the meaning 'more than' (19,8), has the meaning 'much' when used in negative sentences: මම සංහල කම වඩය කනන න. මම ම කම ජත ගන වඩය දනන න. මහතතය වඩය ගදර න. i don't eat much sinhalese food. i don't know much about these kinds of food. the master isn't at home much. 9. ගන ගන 'about, concerning takes a dependent noun in the direct case: වඩ වඩ ගන මකත දනන න. i don't know anything about carpentry. ලමය ගන මකද කරනන? what are you going to do about the boy? 10. 'in sinhalese' 'in a language' is expressed with the instrumental case of the language name: සංහලන නමක න, මහතතය . ඒකට සංහලන කයනන මකකද? මකට සංහලන කයනන මකක ද? there isn't a name (for that) in sinhalese, sir. what is that called in sinhalese? what is this called in sinhalese? [page 347] note that in the sentences above the word for 'this, that' is in the dative case. 11. 'what does it mean?' the common sinhalese expression for 'what does it mean' is තයනන මකක ද? or කයනන මනව ද , preceded by the (sinhalese) word or phrase for which the meaning is being asked. may always be used in such a construction, but the singular: මනව ද only in ප‍රයඩ රයස කයනන මනව ද? what does 'fraid rais' mean? පල ගඩය කයනන මකක ද? what does 'pol gediyə mean? 12. ...08... හර. . 8 is a conjunction with the english equivalent 'either. or'. 8 follows each of the two or more items listed: එලල හර මස හර ගනන. bring (me) either vegetables or meat. එලල කරයක හර මස කරයක හර ඉසස දල කරයක හර හදල දනන පලවන. (i) can make either a vegetable curry, a meat curry, or a curry with shrimp. .හර .8 does not occur in negative statements, but may occur in negative questions: කකල මස හර හරක මස හර නදද? don't you have chicken or beef? 13. a portion with names of foods, as with drinks (16, 11), quantity expres-sions occur implying portions or servings of the food. these follow the normal quantity phrase construction, that is, the noun is plural and the forms ໑໑, ໑໙, etc., are used: [page 348] එලල දක බත දකක කර තන the two (servings of) vegetables two (servings of) rice the three portions of curry parallel to these constructions the form on may be used with the plural form of the name of a food, implying a single portion or serving: එලල එක the serving of vegetables බත එකක a portion of rice කම එකක a meal කර එක the portion of curry 14. the plurals of the a set the plurals of මක 'this one', අරක, ඕක, ඒක that one', are these', 46, ໖໖, 'those'. the case forms are: direct: මව අරව ඕව ඒවට dative: මවට අරවට ඕවට ඒව ඒවය genitive: මවය අරවය ඕවය ඒවයන instrumental: මවයන අරවයන ඕවයන 15. කටර the dative form of a 'everybody, everyone is hence: කවරත යනව. කටත තරනව. everyone is going. everyone understands. 16. ගනත ගනව 'bring' has the alternative past participle forms ca and ගනත hence either: පටන ගනත දනන පලවන. or පටන ගනලල දනන පලවන. [page 349] 17. නතතං when 'if' is added to, the result is නතතං : ම කම කට දනන න. ම කම කට දනන නතතං, තව ටකක කනන. මහතතය සංහල කම කල න. this food isn't hot. if this food isn't hot, eat a bit more. you haven't eaten sinhalese food. මහතතය සංහල කම කල නතතං, අද වත කනන. if you haven't eaten sinhalese food, eat it today at least. exercises a. substitute orally: 1. මට වඩය දනන න. about buses about colombo trains about the work of the estate about sinhalese curries about indian people about pork about hot food about english food about the names of the sinhalese people about food fried in duntel 2. මහතතයට මකත පලවන. bring (for you) pick (for you) prepare (for you) mix (for you) fry (for you) boil (for you) cut (for you) make (for you) [page 350] [page 351] [page 352]

title: LESSON 23
text: LESSON 23 LESSON 23 [page 353] Conversation: Visiting Anuradhapura John Wood visits Anuradhapura with his friend and guide, Gunasena. නුවර අග නුවර වෙලා තිඋනා අනුරාදපුරේ ලංකාවෙ අග නුවර වෙලා තිඋනේ කොයි කාලෙද? JOHN ලංකාවෙ පලවෙනි අග නුවර අනුරාදපුරේ. සතවසෙ සිංහල මිනිස්සු ලංකාවට ආපු කාලෙ ඉඳලා දහවෙනි සතවර්යෙ විතර වෙනකං අග නුවර ති උනේ අනුරාදපුරේ. සිංහලයා බ්‍රිස්තු වර්සෙ සිංහලයො ආවෙ ක්‍රිස්තු වර්සෙන් ඉස්සර, නේද? chief the city the capital had become When was Anuradhapura the capital of Ceylon? GUNASENA Ceylon's first capital was Anuradhapura. the century From the time the Sinhalese came to Ceylon, until about the Tenth Century, the capital was in Anuradhapura. JOHN the Sinhalese (man) the Christian Era The Sinhalese came before the Christian Era, didn't they? [page 354] GUNASENA ඔව්. ක්‍රිස්තු වර්සෙන් ඉස්සර පන්සිය හතලිස් හතරෙදි. Yes, in 544 в.с. JOHN වැව ඒවා the tank, reservoir things මේ වැව් සේරම ඒ කාලෙ කරපු ඒවා ද? Are all these tanks ones built at that time? GUNASENA වැඩි හරිය පුරාන the majority ancient ඔව්. වැව් වලින් වැඩි හරිය බොහොම පුරාන කාලෙ කරපු ඒවා. Yes. The majority of these tanks were built in very ancient times. අනුරාදපුර කාලෙ ඉතාම තමයි the Anuradhapura Period most Indeed අනුරාදපුර කාලෙ තමයි ලංකාවෙ ඉතාම දියුනු කාලෙ. The Anuradhapura Period was the most developed period in Ceylon. අර පේන දාගැබ that over there stupa අර පේන දාගැබ බලන්න. Look at that stupa over there. රුවන්වැලි සෑය ඒක තමයි රුවන්වැලි සෑය. Ruwanweliseya That is the Ruwanwellseya. රජ්ජුරුවො දුටුගැමුනු the king Dutugemunu ඒක හැදුවෙ දුටුගැමුනු රජ්ජුරුවො. It was built by King Dutugemunu. [page 355] JOHN ඒ කොයි කාලෙ ද? When was that? GUNASENA ක්‍රිස්තු වර්සෙන් ඉස්සර දෙවෙනි සතවර්සෙ. In the Second Century, В.С. JOHN සිරිමහ බෝදිය සිරිමහ බෝදිය තියෙන්නෙ කොතෙන්ද? the sacred Bodhi tree Where is the sacred Bodhi tree? GUNASENA හැරෙනවා දකුනට turn to the right අර හන්දියෙන් දකුනට හැරිලා ටිකක් දුර යන්න ඕන. You must turn right from that corner and go a little distance. ඉස්සෙල්ලා first, before everything else අපි ඉස්සෙල්ලා මේ දාගැබ බලමු. INTIMATE EXPRESSIONS Conversation 24, a very informal discussion between two student friends, contains a number of expressions which are suitable for such a situation, but very rarely used in more formal circum-stances. Thus, while the user of the book might wish to know them, he should avoid using them unless he is sure that such informality is allowable. 3.1 ໕໖ is used primarily by young people to equals, either as a term of address or as a form meaning 'you'. It is very common among male college students and school boys. Older people use 1t infrequently, and girls and women very rarely. අයිසේ යනවා ද? Are you going? අයියෙන් එනවා ද? It's enough if you read the books, chum. 3.2 ໙໖໖ is a 'you' form used for equals, or sometimes by a superior to an inferior (except within the family group). Different people have different reactions to it, and its use and implications vary from area to area of Ceylon. Some speakers use it freely while others studiously avoid it. Like 43 it is used mostly by men. The safest rule is not to use it, but not to be offended if others do. [page 378] 3.3 ໖໖໐ is one of the members of the sea set, and thus may mean 'that person by you'. It is also used as an equivalent to 'you'. As such it is primarily restricted to close friends, and is less formal than wed, more so than w. There is some individual variation in the extent to which people use ໖໖ just as there is with ๒๑๕ (6.6). Just as some will use ໖໐໖ where others would continue to use ໑໙໖໐໖, some will use ඔයා, where others would continue to use . As always, it is safest to lean toward greater formality and use ໑໙໙໖ , unless one is sure of the intimacy permitted by the situation, and the impli-cation of the other forms in the particular area and group con-cerned. 4. THE SIMPLE IMPERATIVE The simple form of the verb may be used as an imperative in those social situations in which the word w would be used for 'you'. හොඳයි. තමුසෙ යනවා. Fine, you go. 5. HOPE' 5.1 බලාපොරොත්තුව 'I hope, I expect may be expressed in Sinhalese by මම බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් ඉන්නවා (8,1). This expression may be used with a noun as object, in which case it equates with the English 'I expect, I hope to get', or with an infinitive as object equating with English 'I expect, I hope': වම ලියුමක් බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් ඉන්නවා. I am expecting a letter. වම යන්න බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් ඉන්නවා. I expect to go. In the negative of the present, is substituted for ໑໙໖ as usual, but the instrumental form බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් 1s replaced by the indefinite direct form බලාපොරොත්තුවක්: මම යන්න බලාපොරොත්තුවක් නෑ. I don't expect to go. මම ලියුමක් බලාපොරොත්තුවක් නෑ. I don't expect a letter. [page 379] The past tense and its negative are formed regularly: මම යන්න බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් උන්නා. I expected to go. වම ලියුමක් බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් උන්නා. I expected a letter. ටම යන්න බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් උන්නෙ නෑ. I didn't expect to go. මම ලියුමක් බලාපොරොත්තුවෙන් උන්නෙ නෑ. With verbs: මහත්තයා වැඩ කරනවා ඇති. I have some books. I have enough books. The master works enough. [page 380] 3. Following adjectives: මේ ගේ ලොකු ඇති. ලොකු ඇපි ගෙවල් තියෙනවා නම් මට කියන්න. 4. As an adjective: ඇති පොල් අරගන අනිත් හරිය මෙතනින් දාන්න. This house is big enough. If there are big enough houses, let me know. Take enough coconuts (1.e., as many as you need) and put the rest here. 5. 48 gerund. also occurs in a construction with the past temporal and also occur in this construction, but very rarely. The usual English equivalent is 'it's enough if මම ගියාම ඇති ඔහේ මට සල්ලි දුන්නාම ඇති. දවසක් වැඩ කෙරුවාම ඇති. ඩොට වීරසිංහගෙ පොත කියෙව්වාම ඇති. වැට බැන්දාම මදි. It's enough if I go. .: It's enough if you give me money. If you work one day, it's enough. It's enough if you read Dr. Weerasinghe's book. It's not enough building the fence. 8. කලින් 8.1 ໑໖ may have as English equivalents 'before', earlier' or 'early'. As a postposition meaning 'before' it is an alternative to gස්සර (14,9) or ඉස්සෙල්ලා (20, 10) 'before!, and like ඉස්සර or takes a noun in the dative case: මීට කලින් මීට ඉස්සර ලමයාට කලින් මට යන්න ඕන. ලමයාට ඉස්සර මම යන්න ඕන. before this I must go before the boy. [page 381] 8.2 කලින් may also follow a verb in the infinitive to form the Sinhalese equivalent of English 'before' clauses; and is an alternative for ໖ in these constructions (20, 10): මහත්තයා ගෙදර එන්න කලින් මම අර පොල් කඩන්න ඕන. I must pick those coconuts be-fore the master comes home. 8.3 As an adverb, may have the English equivalent 'earlier' or 'early'; ໘໖ can also be used in this way: කලින් එන්න පුලුවන් නම් හොඳයි. ඉස්සෙල්ලා එන්න පුලුවන් නම් හොඳයි. It will be good if you can come earlier (early). 9. 'THAT'S WHY' ඒක plus the assertion marker may mean 'that's why'. It is used with the emphatic form of the verb: ඒකයි මම ආවේ. අද කොළඹ උත්සවයක් තියෙනවා. That's why I came. There is a festival in Colombo today. මහත්තයා කොළඹ යන්නෙ ඒකයි. That's why the master is going. 10. නැති Some uses of the form of ware parallel to the verbal adjective form of verbs. 10.1 may modify a following noun, and may be accompanied by other elements that accompany it in sentences to form the Sinhalese equivalent of an English negative relative clause (compare the verbal adjectives in 19, 5): ලමයා ඉස්කෝලෙ යන්නෙ නෑ. ඉස්කෝලෙ යන්නෙ නැති ලමයා නෝනා පොත් කියවන්නේ නෑ. නෝනා කියවන්නෙ නැති පොත් The child doesn't go to school. The child who doesn't go to school The mistress doesn't read books. The books the mistress doesn't read [page 382] මම තානායමේ නවතින්නෙ නෑ. මම නවතින්නෙ නැති තානායම I'm not staying in the rest-house. The resthouse that I am not staying in 10.2 From the verbal adjective a verbal noun is formed by adding ໖໖ to it (14, 6). In the same way, a verbal noun may be formed by adding එක to නැති producing නැති එක Like the verbal noun of 14, 6, this is the equivalent of the English verbal noun in "-ing" or an English clause introduced by "that." තමුසෙ හූ කියන්නෙ නෑ. තමුසෙ හු කියන්නෙ නැති එක වැඩියෙ හොඳයි. You don't hoot. It's better that you don't hoot. (Your not hooting is better.) 11. USEFUL EXPRESSIONS 1. ໖ is often used to mean 'otherwise', 'if not', or 'if you don't, if one doesn't', 'why else': නැතුව? Otherwise? Why else? නැතුව මම මොකද කරන්නෙ? Otherwise, what can I do? නැතුව ඉගනගන්නෙ කොහොම ද? If not, how can one learn? 2. ໐ ໑໕໙ 'stay without doing anything' is commonly used in the imperative to stop or discourage someone from doing somethin As such, it may have numerous English equivalents: මහත්තයා නිතං ඉන්න. [page 376] එහනම තමස වනද වනන යනව. gunasena යලව හබය, යලව, මගන අහනන එප කතවට කයප දවල. then you go and enjoy yourself. the friend but, friend, don't ask me the things said in the talk. grammar 1. new nouns class 1 ලකටර එක 'the lecture' class 2 සමතය 'the society, association'; gen, ຜ p1. සරවත රසවම the meeting'; gen. ddd; pl. d໖ කතව 'the talk, lecture; gen. i p1. කත දනවම 'the notice'; gen. ; p1. දනවම මතරකව "the topic'; gen. මරකව; p1. මත රක සහත‍යය 'the literature; gen. ຜບຜ p1. සහත‍ය රවම 'the round, stroll'; gen. ໒໖໖; pl. 693 රසතයදව 'the loafing'; gen. 8; pl. ໒໖ පල හලල 'the useless talk'; gen. ua; pl. class 4 'the examination'; pl. ری 'the question'; pl. ໘໙ දසපලන 'the thing'; pl. 'politics'; (no plural) වනද 'enjoyment'; (no plural) class 5 රසතයදකරය 'the loafer'; pl. යලව 'the friend'; pl. [page 377] 2. new verbs class 1 ගහනව 'hit' කලපන කරනව 'think' පස කරනව 'pass' රසතයද වනව 'loaf' හ කයනව 'boo' අහනව 'listen to (or 'ask' 13,11) irregular හත ගනනව 'have, have in mind, intend' නකං ඉනනව 'stay without doing anything' වනද වනව 'enjoy' 3. intimate expressions conversation 24, a very informal discussion between two student friends, contains a number of expressions which are suitable for such a situation, but very rarely used in more formal circum-stances. thus, while the user of the book might wish to know them, he should avoid using them unless he is sure that such informality is allowable. 3.1 ໕໖ is used primarily by young people to equals, either as a term of address or as a form meaning 'you'. it is very common among male college students and school boys. older people use 1t infrequently, and girls and women very rarely. අයස යනව ද? are you going? අයයන එනව ද? are you coming, too? පත කයවවම ඇත, අයස . it's enough if you read the books, chum. 3.2 ໙໖໖ is a 'you' form used for equals, or sometimes by a superior to an inferior (except within the family group). different people have different reactions to it, and its use and implications vary from area to area of ceylon. some speakers use it freely while others studiously avoid it. like 43 it is used mostly by men. the safest rule is not to use it, but not to be offended if others do. [page 378] 3.3 ໖໖໐ is one of the members of the sea set, and thus may mean 'that person by you'. it is also used as an equivalent to 'you'. as such it is primarily restricted to close friends, and is less formal than wed, more so than w. there is some individual variation in the extent to which people use ໖໖ just as there is with ๒๑๕ (6.6). just as some will use ໖໐໖ where others would continue to use ໑໙໖໐໖, some will use ඔය, where others would continue to use . as always, it is safest to lean toward greater formality and use ໑໙໙໖ , unless one is sure of the intimacy permitted by the situation, and the impli-cation of the other forms in the particular area and group con-cerned. 4. the simple imperative the simple form of the verb may be used as an imperative in those social situations in which the word w would be used for 'you'. හඳය. තමස යනව. fine, you go. 5. hope' 5.1 බලපරතතව 'i hope, i expect may be expressed in sinhalese by මම බලපරතතවන ඉනනව (8,1). this expression may be used with a noun as object, in which case it equates with the english 'i expect, i hope to get', or with an infinitive as object equating with english 'i expect, i hope': වම ලයමක බලපරතතවන ඉනනව. i am expecting a letter. වම යනන බලපරතතවන ඉනනව. i expect to go. in the negative of the present, is substituted for ໑໙໖ as usual, but the instrumental form බලපරතතවන 1s replaced by the indefinite direct form බලපරතතවක: මම යනන බලපරතතවක න. i don't expect to go. මම ලයමක බලපරතතවක න. i don't expect a letter. [page 379] the past tense and its negative are formed regularly: මම යනන බලපරතතවන උනන. i expected to go. වම ලයමක බලපරතතවන උනන. i expected a letter. ටම යනන බලපරතතවන උනන න. i didn't expect to go. මම ලයමක බලපරතතවන උනන න. i didn't expect a letter. 5.2 හතගන ඉනනව හතගන is the past participle of a verb හතගනනව 'to have in mind'. the forms of this verb other than a occur only rarely in certain special situations. the complex verb ໑ ໑໙໖ , may take a dependent infinitive, but not a dependent noun object and may have the same meaning as බලපරතතවන ඉනනව: මට නම යනන හතගන ඉනනව. i, of course, intend to go. මම ම සමන පර ඉවර කරනන හතගන ඉනනව. i hope to finish the road this week. 6. මතක 'remember' 'remember' takes its subject in the dative case and the assertion marker in simple sentences. thus: මට මතකය. මට ඒ තතව මතකය. මට මකත මතක න. i remember. i remember that story. i don't remember anything. 7. ඇත 'enough' 'enough' is like e 'not enough' ໖ 'too much' (22,8). 1. it replaces තයනව , ඉනනව : මට පත තයනව. මට පත ඇත. 2. with verbs: මහතතය වඩ කරනව ඇත. i have some books. i have enough books. the master works enough. [page 380] 3. following adjectives: ම ග ලක ඇත. ලක ඇප ගවල තයනව නම මට කයනන. 4. as an adjective: ඇත පල අරගන අනත හරය මතනන දනන. this house is big enough. if there are big enough houses, let me know. take enough coconuts (1.e., as many as you need) and put the rest here. 5. 48 gerund. also occurs in a construction with the past temporal and also occur in this construction, but very rarely. the usual english equivalent is 'it's enough if මම ගයම ඇත ඔහ මට සලල දනනම ඇත. දවසක වඩ කරවම ඇත. ඩට වරසංහග පත කයවවම ඇත. වට බනදම මද. it's enough if i go. .: it's enough if you give me money. if you work one day, it's enough. it's enough if you read dr. weerasinghe's book. it's not enough building the fence. 8. කලන 8.1 ໑໖ may have as english equivalents 'before', earlier' or 'early'. as a postposition meaning 'before' it is an alternative to gසසර (14,9) or ඉසසලල (20, 10) 'before!, and like ඉසසර or takes a noun in the dative case: මට කලන මට ඉසසර ලමයට කලන මට යනන ඕන. ලමයට ඉසසර මම යනන ඕන. before this i must go before the boy. [page 381] 8.2 කලන may also follow a verb in the infinitive to form the sinhalese equivalent of english 'before' clauses; and is an alternative for ໖ in these constructions (20, 10): මහතතය ගදර එනන කලන මම අර පල කඩනන ඕන. i must pick those coconuts be-fore the master comes home. 8.3 as an adverb, may have the english equivalent 'earlier' or 'early'; ໘໖ can also be used in this way: කලන එනන පලවන නම හඳය. ඉසසලල එනන පලවන නම හඳය. it will be good if you can come earlier (early). 9. 'that's why' ඒක plus the assertion marker may mean 'that's why'. it is used with the emphatic form of the verb: ඒකය මම ආව. අද කලඹ උතසවයක තයනව. that's why i came. there is a festival in colombo today. මහතතය කලඹ යනන ඒකය. that's why the master is going. 10. නත some uses of the form of ware parallel to the verbal adjective form of verbs. 10.1 may modify a following noun, and may be accompanied by other elements that accompany it in sentences to form the sinhalese equivalent of an english negative relative clause (compare the verbal adjectives in 19, 5): ලමය ඉසකල යනන න. ඉසකල යනන නත ලමය නන පත කයවනන න. නන කයවනන නත පත the child doesn't go to school. the child who doesn't go to school the mistress doesn't read books. the books the mistress doesn't read [page 382] මම තනයම නවතනන න. මම නවතනන නත තනයම i'm not staying in the rest-house. the resthouse that i am not staying in 10.2 from the verbal adjective a verbal noun is formed by adding ໖໖ to it (14, 6). in the same way, a verbal noun may be formed by adding එක to නත producing නත එක like the verbal noun of 14, 6, this is the equivalent of the english verbal noun in "-ing" or an english clause introduced by "that." තමස හ කයනන න. තමස හ කයනන නත එක වඩය හඳය. you don't hoot. it's better that you don't hoot. (your not hooting is better.) 11. useful expressions 1. ໖ is often used to mean 'otherwise', 'if not', or 'if you don't, if one doesn't', 'why else': නතව? otherwise? why else? නතව මම මකද කරනන? otherwise, what can i do? නතව ඉගනගනන කහම ද? if not, how can one learn? 2. ໐ ໑໕໙ 'stay without doing anything' is commonly used in the imperative to stop or discourage someone from doing somethin as such, it may have numerous english equivalents: මහතතය නතං ඉනන. don't do it. එහනම තමස නකං ඉනනව. all right, stay then! ලමය, නකං ඉනන. don't bother me, child. [page 383]

title: Lesson 25
text: Lesson 25 Lesson 25 [page 1] Conversation: Running for Office Perera tries to talk Gunapala into running for Parliament in the next election. PERERA පාර්ලිමේන්තුව Parliament ඉදිරිපත් වෙනවා come forward නරක bad මහත්තයාටත් නරක ද මේ පාර පාර්ලිමේන්තුවට ඉදිරිපත් උනොත්? Why don't you run for Parliament this time? GUNAPALA දැනට right now එහෙම like that කල් time දැනට නම් එහෙම බලාපොරොත්තුවක් නෑ. Right now, I don't have any such intention. නමුත් තව කල් තියෙනවා, නේ ? But there's still time, isn't there? PERERA පුලුවන්කව possibility සලකලා බලනවා consider පුලුවන්කමක් තියෙනවා නම් සලකලා බලන්න. If there is a possibility, do consider it. ඕන කරන become necessary ගම්මු villagers බලාපොරොත්තු වෙනවා expect [page 2] ඕන කරන උදව්වක් ගම්මුන්ගෙන් බලාපොරොත්තු වෙන්න පුලුවනි. ඇහුනා ද? You can expect any help you need from the villagers. All right? (Literally: Did you hear?) GUNAPALA ඒ උනාට nevertheless මහ great, big ඒ උනාට ඒක මහ කරදර වැඩේ, නේ. Nevertheless, that's a very tedious job, isn't it? රෑ දවල් day and night ගෙයක් ගානෙ house to house ඇවදිනවා walk මහන්සි වෙනවා exert oneself, tire oneself රෑ දවල් ගෙයක් ගානෙ ඇවිදින්නයි කතා කරන්නයි කොචිවර මහන්සි වෙන්න ඕනද? NEGATIVE FORMATION -නෙවී Up to this point, negative sentences or clauses, except those with එපා and බෑ have been formed with නෑ or one of its forms (නැති, නැත්තෙ, නැතුව and the interrogative නැද්ද). In this conversation, the other major Sinhalese negative word, නෙවී, occurs for the first time. නෙවී forms the negative of some important sentence types for which නෑ may not be used, and hence for which negative forms have not been given so far. 3.1 Equational sentences with a noun or noun phrase as predicate attribute regularly form the negative by adding නෙවී : මේක හොඳ සිගරැට් ජාතියක් නෙවී . This is not a good kind of cigarette. අර කවුන්ටරේ පොත් නවකතා පොත් නෙවී . The books on that counter are not novels. ඒක හැබෑව නෙව් . That's not so. චන්දය දිනන එක ලේසි වැඩක් නෙවී . Winning a vote isn't an easy job. 3.2 Emphatic sentences form the negative by adding නෙවී: මහත්තයා යන්නෙ කලුතරට නෙවී . It's not to Kalutara that the master is going. මම කිව්වෙ ඒක නෙවී . That isn't what I said! අර දොස්තර එලවන්නේ ඔස්ටන් එකක් නෙවී . It isn't an Austin that that doctor drives. මට ඕන මස් කරියක් නෙවී . It isn't a meat curry I want. Note that a negative sentence with නෙවී usually implies that the speaker, in denying something, has another alternative in mind. Hence the alternative may be expressed: [page 7] මේක මගේ පොත නෙවී , මහත්තයාගෙ පොත . This isn't my book. It's the gentleman's book. චන්දයක් දිනන එක ලේසි වැඩක් නෙවී , බොහොම අමාරු වැඩක් . Winning a vote isn't an easy job, it's very hard. මහත්තයා යන්නෙ අනුරාදපුරේට නෙවී , සීගිරියට . The master isn't going to Anuradhapura, but to Sigiriya. මට ඕන හරක් මස් නෙවී , කුකුල් මස් . It isn't a beef curry I want, but a chicken (curry). 3.3 In some dialects of Sinhalese, නෙවී occurs as නෙමෙ, but there is no difference in use: මේක හොඳ සිගරැට් ජාතියක් නෙමෙ . This is not a good kind of cigarette. මහත්තයා යන්නෙ කලුතරට නෙමෙ . It's not to Kalutara that the master is going. 4. THE මෙහෙම SET 4.1 එහෙම 'like that' is one of another set of four location words: මෙහෙම like this ඔහොම like that (which you are doing, or which involves you) අරහෙම like that (over there) එහෙම like that (in question) In previous lessons, එහෙම has occurred in such expressions as: එහෙම ද ? (Is it) like that? Is that so? එහෙම නම් If it's like that if that's so The other members of the set occur in similar expressions. For example: මෙහෙමද ? Like this? Is it like this? මෙහෙම නම් If it's like this if this is so [page 8] 4.2 The members of the set occur adverbially, with the meaning 'like this, like that', or 'in this, that way', 'so': ඔහොම ලියන්න එපා ; මෙහෙම ලියන්න . Don't write like that (as you are), write like this! තාත්තාට ඔහොම කතා කරන්න එපා ! Don't talk to your father that way! වන්ද එහෙම දිනන්න බෑ . You can't win votes like that (in that way). එහෙම කරලාත් මට වන්ද දිනාගන්න බෑ . Even having done so, I can't win those votes. 4.3 They may also act as adjectives modifying following nouns, and may have English equivalents 'like this/that' or 'of this/that sort'. මෙහෙම කෑම මම කවදාවත් කාලා නෑ . I've never eaten food like this. අරහෙම පොත් කියවන්න ඔහේට පුලුවන්ද ? Can you read books of that sort? 4.4 කොහොම 'how, in what way' is the corresponding interrogative word to the මෙහෙම set: මෙහෙමද ? Like this? කොහොම ද ? How? මේ වැඩ කරන්නෙ මෙහෙමද ? Is this work done in this way? මේ වැඩ කරන්නෙ කොහොමද ? How is this work done? 5. COMPLEX VERBS 5.1 In Lesson 22, we met complex verbs formed with a past participle plus දෙනවා. As noted there, these complex verbs usually have the sense 'to do something for someone'. Thus: මට කරියක් හදලා දෙන්න . Make me a curry. මට ටැක්සියක් නවත්තලා දෙන්න . Stop a taxi for me. අපිට වැටක් බැඳලා දුන්නා . (He) built us a fence. [page 9] These complex verbs with දෙනවා, if they are formed with the past participles of Class 1 or Class 2 verbs, have alternative forms which may occur with no change of meaning. These alternate forms have the PAST PARTICIPLE STEM rather than the past participle. The past participle stem is that to which either -ලා the of the past participle or the -පු of the past participial adjective is added. Thus, instead of the sentences above, we may have: මට කරියක් හදා දෙන්න . Make me a curry. ටැක්සියක් නවත්තා දෙන්න . Stop a taxi for me. මට අපිට වැටක් බැඳ දුන්නා . (He) built us a fence. It will be remembered that Class 1 verbs have alternate past participle forms with either ə or aa , a so that හදනවා has either හදලා or හදාලා; නවත්තනවා either නවත්තලා or නවත්තාලා. They thus have alternate forms of the past participle stem. However, only the form with -a- or -aa- occurs as the first member of complex verbs, never the form with -ə . Class 3 verbs do not occur in complex verb constructions. 5.2 Complex verbs may also be formed with ගන්නවා, but these always have the form past participial stem plus ගන්නවා. There is no alternative form with the past participle. The meaning is most commonly 'to do for oneself'. Thus: මම කරියක් හදාගන්නවා . I'm making myself a curry. මම ටැක්සියක් නවත්තාගන්නම් . I'll stop a taxi (for myself). මේ මිනිස්සුන්ගේ චන්ද ලබාගන්න අමාරුයි . It's hard to get these people's votes. 6. EXCLAMATORY SENTENCES Sentences with an interrogative word and ද may be exclamatory as well as interrogative: මේ බඩු වලට කොච්චර සල්ලි ඕන ද ? How much money do I need for these goods? මේ බඩු වලට කොච්චර සල්ලි ඕන ද ! How much money I need for these goods! [page 10] පාර්ලිමේන්තුවට ඉදිරිපත් වෙන්න කොච්චර මහන්සි වෙන්න ඕනද? How much effort must one ex-pend to run for Parliament? පාර්ලිමේන්තුවට ඉදිරිපත් වෙන්න කොච්චර මහන්සි වෙන්න ඕන ද! How much effort one must ex-pend to run for Parliament! 7. වත් වත් 'even, at least' commonly has the English equivalent 'at least' in positive and 'even' in negative sentences. 7.1 වත් may follow a noun: මට හෙට වත් යන්න ඕන . I want to go tomorrow, at least මට හෙට වත් යන්න ඕන නෑ . Even tomorrow, I don't want to go. එහේ හෝටලේ බත් වත් තියෙනවා . In the hotel there there's rice at least. එහේ හෝටලේ බත් වත් නෑ . In the hotel there there's not even rice. 7.2 2 may occur after an infinitive accompanying පුලුවන් or බැ. මට පයින් වත් යන්න පුලුවනි . I can at least go on foot. මට පයින් වත් යන්න බෑ . I can't even go on foot. හිතන්න වත් බෑ 'can't even think, imagine' is an example of this construction, but with an infinitive dependent on හිතන්න it takes on the idiomatic sense 'haven't the slightest chance of': එහෙම කරලත් සමහරුන්ට ආසනයක් දිනා ගන්න හිතන්න වත් බෑ . And even having done so, some haven't the slightest chance of winning a seat. 8. තිඋනාට මදි. In Lesson 24 we met a construction with the past temporal gerund and ඇති (and rarely මදි or වැඩි) as in: පොත් කියෙව්වාම ඇති . Reading books is enough. [page 11] In this conversation a similar construction occurs, in which the simple past tense of the verb inflected for dative case is used rather than the gerund; in this construction only මදි is used. මහජනයාට හිතවත්කම තිඋනාට මදි. Having the public's interest at heart isn't enough. ගං සබාවෙ කටයුතු කෙරුවාට මදි. Having carried out village committee duties isn't enough. 9. පුලුවන් කම තම may be added to forms like පුලුවන්, බෑ (in the form බැරි), ඕන, එපා, නැ (in the form නැති), as well as to a number of adjectives to form nouns with a related meaning. පුලුවන් කම the possibility බැරි කම the impossibility ඕන කම the necessity එපා කම the lack of interest නැති කම the lack පුලුවන්කමක් තියෙනවා නම් සලකලා බලන්න . If there is a possibility, think it over. යන්න ඕනකම නිසා මම කුලී කාර් එකක් ගත්තා . Because of my desire to go, I got a taxi. These nouns inflect like Class 2 nouns: එයාට කාර් එක එලවන්න බැරිකමෙන් ගමන පරක්කු උනා . The trip was delayed (i.e., it took longer) because he couldn't drive a car. 10. ගාන ගානෙ preceded by a noun in the direct indefinite forms the Sinhalese equivalent of such expressions as 'from house to house', 'from village to village', 'day after day'. ගෙයක් ගානෙ යන්න ඕන . We must go from house to house. උන්නැහේ දවසක් ගානේ ලැක්ටර් කරනවා . He lectures day after day. [page 12] අපි ගමක් ගානෙ ගියා . We went from village to village. Optionally, the noun in the indefinite may be repeated with no change in meaning: ගෙයක් ගෙයක් ගානෙ from house to house දවසක් දවසක් ගාන day after day ගමක් ගමක් ගාන from village to village In all the above expressions, the word ගානෙ may be replaced by පාසා with no change in meaning: ගෙයක් පාසා ගෙයක් ගෙයක් පාසා from house to house 11. කිසිම 'any … at all' කිසිම modifies following nouns in the indefinite, and the resulting phrase may occur only in a negative sentence. The sense is 'any … at all' or 'a single …': මේ ලමයාට කිසිම පොතක් නෑ The boy doesn't have a single book. වත්තෙ කිසිම මිනිහෙක් නෑ . There aren't any men at all in the estate. අපි ලඟ කිසිම සිගරැට් ජාතියක් නෑ . We don't have any kinds of cigarettes at all. මෙහේ කිසිම කෙනෙක් නෑ . There's nobody here at all. 12. හිතවත් හිතවත් is an adjective with the meaning 'thinking of someone's or something's interest', or 'having it at heart'. The beneficiary is in the dative case: ඒ මහජනයාට හිතවත් කෙනෙක් . That's a man who has the public's interest at heart! කම may be added to හිතවත් to form a related noun හිතවත්කම 'the having of X's interest at heart'. [page 13] මහජනයාට හිතවත්කම තිඋනාට මදි . Having the public's interest at heart isn't enough. ඔහේට හිතවත්කම තියෙන කෙනෙකුට කියන්න . Tell (it) to a person who has your interest at heart. 13. වගේ 13.1 In Lesson 19, phrases with a 'like' and a dependent noun in the direct case occurred as predicate attributes. The asser-tion marker is optional: ඒ මිනිහා මහත්තයා වගේ . That man is like the master. Such phrases may, like adjectives, modify following nouns and, as with adjectives, the assertion marker does not appear: මහත්තයා වගේ කෙනෙක් ඕන . We want a man like you. 13.2 වගේ may be used with a preceding dependent noun or pronoun to form an adverbial construction. The case of the dependent noun or pronoun will depend on the construction in which it is used: අර මහත්තයාට වගේ මටත් සිංහල පුලුවනි . I can speak Sinhalese like that gentleman. මහත්තයාගෙ වගේ පොතක් පිටත් තියෙනවා . I have a book like yours. 14. 'BAD FOR' In Sinhalese, the equivalent of the English 'bad for somebody' Is expressed by the dative case of the person plus the adjective නරක 'bad'. Equivalent expression may be formed with many adjectives: මහත්තයාට නරක ද ? Would (it) be bad for you? මේ කෑම මට හොඳ නෑ . This food isn't good for me. මේ වැඩ මට අමාරුයි . This work is hard for me. මේ වැඩ මට පහසුයි . This work is easy for me. මේ පොත මට ප්‍රයෝජනවත් . This book is useful to me. [page 14] 15. දැනට දැනට is the word 'now' with the dative case ending added to it, and has the meaning 'right now', 'at this time'. දැනට එහෙම බලාපොරොත්තුවක් නෑ . At this time, I have no such intention. 16. ඒ උනාට ඒ උනාට 'nevertheless, but' is used like නමුත් but can have only the meaning 'but, not, nevertheless': ඒ උනාට මට යන්න පුලුවනි . But I can go. නමුත් මට යන්න පුලුවනි . But I can go. 17. 'THROUGHOUT' The post position තිස්සෙ takes a noun in the direct case and has the meaning 'throughout'. It has a variant form මුලුල්ලෙ: මම මාසයක් තිස්සෙ මෙහෙ උන්නා . I stayed here (throughout) a month. මම මාසයක් මුලුල්ලේ මෙහෙ උන්නා . I stayed here (throughout) a month. 18. 'TIME' The words කල් and වෙලා both may equate with English 'time' in expressions such as 'a lot of time'. වෙලා usually means a short period of time, something less than a day, and කල් a longer stretch: මට වැඩ කරන්න කල් මදි . I don't have enough time to work. මට වැඩ කරන්න වෙලා මදි . I don't have enough time to work. කල් is actually the plural form of the Class 3 noun කල 'the time', but the latter is used only in some special situations, to be learned as they occur.
