[page 51] emphatic මම ලඟ ඇතත ත‍රරස සගරට . three roses cigarettes are the ones i might have (in my shop). 4. past tense verbal adjective 4.1 sinhalese has a past tense verbal adjective formed for all classes by substituting -ə for -a in the past tense simple form; that is, in terms of sinhalese writing, removing the  from the past tense simple form: verb past simple form past verbal adjective class 1 cut කපනව කපව කපව look, see බලනව බලව බලව class 2 draw, pull අදනව ඇදද ඇදද fry බදනව බදද බදද class 3 understand තරනව තරන තරන turn හරනව හරන හරන irregular go යනව ගය ගය come එනව ආව ආව 4.2 the past tense verbal adjective is used to modify a following noun with the same implication as the past participial adjective (22, 5): බංඩ ඊය කඩප පල ගනන . බංඩ ඊය කඩව පල ගනන . bring the coconuts that banda picked yesterday. other examples are: සඳද ගය මහතතය මම දනනව . i know the man who went on monday. [page 52] ගනසංහ ලවව පත පට වල තයනව . the book gunasinha wrote has come out. මම ඒ මනහට දනන සලල දකක ද ? did you see the money i gave that man? 5. verbal nouns sinhalese has three types of verbal nouns: 5.1 verbal nouns in -iimə or -illə : a verbal noun is formed from the past tense stem of classes 1 and 3 by dropping the final -u- or -un- of the past tense stem and adding the suffix -iimə or -illə . from verbs of class 2 a verbal noun is formed by adding the same suffix -iimə or -illə to the past tense stem, but without the doubling of the last consonant of the stem. verb past tense past tense stem verbal noun class 1 cut කපනව කපව කප - කපම , කපලල the cutting make හදනව හදව හද - හදම , හදලල the making teach උගනනනව ඉගනනව ඉගනන - ඉගන නම , ඉගනනලල the teaching class 2 pull, draw අදනව ඇදද ඇදද - ඇදම , ඇදලල the pulling bind, erect බඳනව බනද බන ද - බඳම , බඳලල the binding class 3 understand තරනව තරන තර - තරම , තරලල the understanding fall වටනව වටන වට - වටම , වටලල the falling [page 53] for the irregular verbs that have occurred so far, the verbal noun forms are: <whole table below good> verb past tense verbal noun ඉනනව උනන ඉඳම , ඉඳලල the being එනව ආව ඒම the coming කනව කව කම , කවලල the eating ගනනව ගතත ගනයම the taking, buying ගනයනව ගනව ගනම , ගනලල the taking ගවදනව ගවදන ගවදම , ගවදලල the settling down ගනව ගනව ගනම , ගනලල the bringing තයනව තඋන ත ම , තබම the being දනව දව ද ම , දවලල the burning දනව දනන දම , දවලල the giving යනව ගය යම , යවලල the going නවතනව නවතන නවතම , නවතලල the staying පනව පනන පනම , පනලල the seeing බනව බවව බම the drinking the verbal noun in -iimə or -illə frequently equates with an english verbal noun in -ing: මන භග ලවම හඳ න . his (hand) writing is no good. බස එලවලලට ක දනක ඕනද ? how many people do you want for driving buses? 5.2 verbal nouns with වග or බව a verbal noun may be formed by following the present verbal adjective, the past verbal adjective, or the past participial adjective with either of the forms වග or බව: with the present verbal adjective: verb verbal noun eat කනව කන වග or කන බව fry බදනව බදන වග or බදන බව understand තරනව තරන වග or තරන බව [page 54] with the past verbal adjective: verb verbal noun eat කනව කව වග or කව බව fry බදනව බදද වග or බදද බව understand තරනව තරන වග or තරන බව with the past participial adjective: eat කනව කප වග, කප බව fry බදනව බදප වග, බදප බව understand තරනව තරචච වග, තරචච බව the verbal noun in වග or බව is used mostly as the object of a verb, and is likely to equate with an english ‘that’ clause or with an english clause introduced by ‘the fact that’: මන හ පත ලයන බව දනනව . මන හ පත ලයන වග දනනව . (i) know that he writes books. එය වඩ කරප බව මහතතය කවව . එය වඩ කරප වග මහතතය කවව . the master said that he worked. note that the form referring to the person performing the action of a verb noun in -iimə , -illə is in the genitive case, whereas one referring to a person performing the action of a verbal noun in වග or බව is in the case normally required as subject by the verb being used: මග ලවම my writing මම ලයන වග that i am writing, or the fact that i am writing මට තරන වග the fact that i understand. 5.3 a verbal noun may be formed by adding එක to the present, past, or past participial verbal adjective. [page 55] with the present verbal adjective: verb verbal noun eat කනව කන එක fry බදනව බදන එක understand තරනව තරන එක with the past verbal adjective: eat කනව ක එක fry බදනව බදද එක understand තරනව තරන එක with the past participial verbal adjective: eat කනව කප එක fry බදනව බදප එක understand තරනව තරචච එක the verbal noun in එක can usually be used in either of the constructions mentioned above. that is, යන එක may mean ‘the going’ or ‘that he is going, the fact that he is going’. how-ever, the form referring to the person who performs the action of the verbal noun must, as in the case of බව , වග be in the case required as subject of the verb: ඒ මනහ පත ලයන එක හඳ න . it isn't good that he writes books. (the fact that he writes books isn't good.) ගනසංහ රසසවන රසසවට මරවන එකට කමත න . (i) don't like gunasinha's going from job to job. උනනහ ලවව එක හර න . it's not proper that he wrote. අසනප නම පයන යන එක හඳ න . if you are ill it's bad to walk. මනහ පත ගනප එක හඳ න . it isn't good that the man brought books. 6. repetition of adjectives 6.1 adjectives preceding a noun may be repeated (’reduplicated’) to give a sense like that of english ‘various’ plus adjective. [page 56] the noun must be plural: හඳ හඳ පත various good books රස රස කම various tasty foods පරන පරන සදදසතන various ancient holy places පත ලයන කට වනස වනස අදහස වනස වනස වදවලට ප‍රකස කරනන පලවන , න ? when you are writing books, various different ideas can be expressed in various different ways, can't they? predicate adjectives are never reduplicated. 6.2 verbal adjectives, in any tense, may also be reduplicated. the usual english equivalent is 'every…'. the noun may be either singular definite or plural with no change in meaning: මනහ ලයන ලයන පත හඳය . every book he writes is good. ඒ ලමය කරන කරන වඩ මටත කරනන පලවන . every job that boy does i can do, too. මම බලව බලව තන ලසසනය . every place i saw was beautiful. නන හදප හදප කරය කට දව . every curry she made was hot. 7. 'from day to day' 'from day to day', 'house to house', etc., may be expressed in sinhalese with the indefinite of the noun plus ගන (25,10). දවසක ගන from day to day ගයක ගන from house to house sinhalese has another way of expressing this. a noun in the instrumental case is followed by the dative case form of the same noun: ගයන ගට from house to house හනදයන හනදයට from corner to corner ගහන ගහට from tree to tree පයන පයට from hour to hour [page 57] however, if the noun involved refers to a period of time of a day or longer, the instrumental form of the noun is followed by the direct form: දවසන දවස from day to day සමනන සමන from week to week අවරදදන අවරදද from year to year 8. ‘two fifty’ the sinhalese equivalent of ‘two fifty’, ‘three forty’ etc., in counting money, quoting prices and telling time is expressed by adding a to the first numeral: දකය පනහ two fifty (two rupees and fifty cents or 2:50 o’clock) තනය හතලහ three forty these phrases take case and definiteness endings and the assertion marker in the same way as single numerals: දහතරය දහයය . its (price is) fourteen ten. දන තනය හතලහය . it’s now 3:40 o’clock. දකය පනහට එනන . come at 2:50. මහතතය හතරය වස පහක දනන . the master gave me four (rupees and) twenty-five (cents). when it is necessary to specify the units of money involved, quantity phrases with the appropriate noun may be joined in the same way as numerals alone: රපයල දකය සත පනහක දනන . give two rupees and fifty cents. මක රපයල හතරය සත දහයය . this one is four rupees and ten cents. ගනසංහ රපයල දහතරය සත පනහක බඩ ගතත . gunasinha bought fourteen rupees and fifteen cents worth of goods. [page 58] 9. ‘before, after’ the postpositions ඉසසලල: ‘before’ and ‘after’ are used with a dependent noun or pronoun in the dative case (14, 9; 16, 9; 20, 10; 23, 7): වසසට ඉසසර ගදර යනන . go home before the rain. ලවමට ??? ඉසසලල කලපන කරනන . think (about it) before you write. මම ගය මහතතයට පසස . i went after you. වට බඳලලට පසස මම වඩ කරනන ගය . after building the fence, i went to work. while පසස may be used with a verbal noun, as above, it is more customary to use it with the dative case of the simple past tense of a verb, with no difference in meaning: වට බනදට පසස මම වඩ කරනන ගය . after building the fence, i went to work. similarly, ඉසසලල and ඉසසර are more commonly used with a dependent infinitive than they are with a verbal noun: ලයනන ඉසසලල කලපන කරනන . think (about it) before you write. ලංකවට යනන ඉසසර සංහල ටකක ඉගන ගනන ඕන . you should learn some sinhalese before going to ceylon. 10. ‘way, manner’ the form වදය ‘the way, manner’ is used in the dative case where english uses ‘in a way’: ම වදයට වඩ කරනන එප . don't work in this way. මම ලයන වදයට ලයනන බර ද ? can't you write the way i write? 11. ‘as’ හටයට හටයට equates with english ‘as, in the capacity of’: මන හ ගරවරයක හටයට වඩය ප‍රසදදය . he is more famous as a teacher. [page 59] ඩ‍රයවර කනක හටයට වඩ කරනන පලවන ද ? can you work as a driver? 12. negative for some adjectives a negative form is made by prefixing අ . there are sometimes changes in the stem when this prefix is added: කමත like අකමත don’t like, dislike සනතස pleased අසනතස not pleased ප‍රයජනවත useful අප‍රයජනවත not useful 13. මං මං is an alternative form for මම ‘i’. it generally implies greater informality: මම යනව . මං යනව . i am going. 14. ‘i think ...’ in sinhalese, both මං හතනන (or මම හතනන) and මග කලපනව equate with english ‘i think (that); my idea is that…’ the subordinate clause may follow these expressions without any introductory conjunction: මං හතනන උනනහ ගරවරයක . i think he’s a teacher. මනහග කලපනව වඩ නකර ගදර යනන . his idea is to go home without doing work. 15. respectful forms the form වරය (plural වර) may be added to many nouns to make a term of respect. when this is added to a noun, it is the වරය that is in inflected, and not the form to which it is added. some nouns never occur without this suffix; for example, ‘teacher’, since this is always used as a term of respect. in other cases, the plural වර may be added to a noun to form an alternative respectful plural even though it is not customary to use වරය in the singular; for example දසතර 'doctor' [page 60] දසතරල or දසතරවර. the noun හමදරව monk' always has the plural form හමදරවර

title: Lesson 29
text: Lesson 29 Lesson 29 [page 69] Grammar 1. NEW NOUNS Class 1 නර්ස්හෝම් එක 'nursing home' ඇපොයින්ට්ස්ට්මන්ට් එක 'appointment' [page 70] Class 2 අමාරුව 'ailment', gen. අමාරුවෙ و pl. අමාරු පපුව 'body', gen. ඇගේ pl. ඇගවල් වාට්ටුව 'chest', gen. පපුවෙ pl. og 'ward', gen. 'pleasure, gen. සතුටෙ pl. වාට්ටු no pl. සතුට Class 4 ඉස්පිරිතාලෙ 'hospital', pl. ඉස්පිරිතාල Class 5 අම්මා 'mother'; indef. අම්මා කෙනෙක් pl. අම්මාලා අයියා 'older brother!; අයියා කෙනෙක් pl. අයියාලා මල්ලී younger brother'; pl. මල්ලිලා අක්කා 'older sister'; අක්කා කෙනෙක් pl. අක්කාලා නංගි 'younger sister'; pl. නංගිලා විසේසඥයා 'specialist', pl. විසේසඥයො 2. NEW VERBS Class 1 ගෙවනවා 'pay' කල්පනා කරනවා 'think' බේත් කරනවා 'give medical treatment' Class 3 රිදෙනවා 'ache' හැදෙනවා 'get (diseases)' Irregular ඇතුල් වෙනවා පරීක්සා කරවා ගන්නවා රස්තියාදු වෙනවා 'enter', past 4 c 'get onself examined', past ໖໖ ໑໒໙໖ 'waste time', past ໒໖ ທ [page 71] 3. INFINITIVE Some speakers of Sinhalese, like Perera in this lesson, have an alternate form of the infinitive with -න්ඩ rather than -න්න. Thus යන්ඩ, වෙන්ඩ, කන්ඩ rather than යන්න, වෙන්න, කන්න. This is especially common in the Colombo area. In other areas, particularly the upcountry, one may encounter -න්ට rather than -න්න. Hence යන්ට, වෙන්ට, කන්ට. Note that in either case, other verb forms with -න්න, such as the emphatic and -න්නම් forms, are not affected and will have -න්න even if the infinitive has -න්ඩ or -න්ට. 4. ‘HAVE ΤΟ’ වෙනවා may be used with a dependent infinitive and dative case subject with the meaning ‘have to’. වෙනවා may appear in most of its inflected forms. When it is in the simple form, the meaning is future: ‘will have to’. මට හෙට කොළඹ යන්න වෙනවා . I will have to go to Colombo tomorrow. පෙරේරා උන්නැහේ එන්නෙ නැත්තං මට ඒ වැඩ කරන්ඩ වෙනවා . If Mr. Perera doesn't come, I'll have to do the work. With other inflected forms of වෙනවා, the meaning will depend on the particular form involved: මට ඊයෙ ගමට යන්න උනා . I had to go to the village yesterday. මිස්ට ගුනසේකරට වත්තක් ගන්න වේවී . Mister Gunasekara might have to buy an estate. මට ඉස්පිරිතාලෙට ඇතුල්වෙන්ඩ උනොත් පවුලට සල්ලි හම්බවෙන්නෙ කොහෙන් ද ? If I have to go to the hospital, where will (my) family get money from? මහත්තයාට රස්සාවට යන්න උනාම මම පවුල බලාගන්න ගෙදර නැවතුනා . When the master had to go to work, I stayed home to take care of the family. [page 72] This construction generally differs in meaning from the similar one with a dependent infinitive plus තියෙනවා (12,7) in that the construction with වෙනවා implies that the situation involved comes about without prior arrangement, or involuntarily, while that with තියෙනවා suggests that the situation has been prearranged or is settled: මට ඊයෙ කොළඹ ඉන්ඩ තිඋනා . I was supposed to be in Colombo yesterday. මහත්තයා ආ නිසා මට ඊයෙ කොළඹ ඉන්න උනා . Because the master came, I had to go to Colombo yesterday. 5. ‘FROM … TO …’ The English ‘from … to … ’ with time expressions is expressed in Sinhalese by … ඉඳලා … වෙන කං. The form dependent upon ඉඳලා is in the genitive case as learned earlier, and the form dependent upon වෙන කං is in the direct case, since වෙන කං means literally ‘till it gets to be’. දවල් දොලහෙ ඉඳලා එක වෙන කං From twelve noon to one. හවස පහේ ඉඳලා හය වෙන කං From five in the afternoon until six. රෑ දෙකේ ඉඳලා එලි වෙන කං From two a.m. (literally two at night) until dawn. The English ‘from … to …’ with place expressions is stated in Sinhalese, as learned in the first lesson, by putting the place to which in the dative case: මෙහේ ඉඳලා කලුතරට From here to Kalutara. 6. කලේ Some of the past tense forms of කරනවා have alternate forms with a past tense stem කල්- rather than කෙරු -. There is no difference in usage or meaning. The alternate forms are: [page 73] කලා = කෙරුවා (simple past) කලේ = කෙරුවෙ (emphatic past) කල = කෙරුව (past tense verbal adjective) කලොත් = කෙරුවොත් (conditional) 7. EMPHATIC EQUATIONAL SENTENCES When an equational sentence with an adjective as predicate attribute is transformed to the emphatic form, the assertion marker is removed from the adjective. As with other emphatic sentences, the emphasized item is frequently put last in the sentence but need not be: Simple: මේ පොත හොඳයි . This book is good. Emphatic: හොඳ මේ පොත . It is this book which is good. As in other types of emphatic sentences, the emphasized form may be further emphasized by adding to it an item such as තමයි or යි: Simple: මහත්තයා ගෙදරට ගිහින් හම්බවෙන එක වැඩියෙ හොඳයි . Your going to (his) house and meeting (him) is better. Emphatic: මහත්තයා ගෙදරට ගිහින් හම්බවෙන එක තමයි වැඩියෙ හොඳ . It is better that you go to his house and meet him. } 8. ADVERBS IN -0 A few adjectives in Sinhalese may add to form an adverb. They must be learned as they occur. The only one that has occurred so far is a 'private'; thus a 'privately'. 2. පුද්ගලිකව වැඩ කරන අයත් ඉන්නවා. No, there are also people who work privately. 9. THIRD PERSON PRONOUNS The plural of the third person pronouns ໑໖໖, ඔයා අරයා, එයා The, she' has been given as මෙයාලා, ඔයාලා, අරයාලා, එයාලා 'they' (11, 3). Another set of third person plural pronouns, [page 74] with no difference in meaning, may be formed by adding di-rectly to the members of the 6 set. Thus: මේ ගොල්ල they (by me) මෙයාලා ඔය ගොල්ල they (by you) = ඔයාලා අර ගොල්ල they (over there) = අරයාලා ඒ ගොල්ල they (in question) = එයාලා Class 5 case endings are added to the forms. Either singular or plural case forms may be used with no difference in meaning. Thus: Direct: මේ ගොල්ල Dative: මේ ගොල්ලට, මේ ගොල්ලන්ට Genitive: මේ ගොල්ලගෙ, මේ ගොල්ලන්ගෙ Instrumental: මේ ගොල්ලගෙන්, මේ ගොල්ලන්ගෙන් 10. රිදෙනවා When the subject of 36໙໖ : 'to hurt, ache' is in the direct case, it expresses that which hurts or aches (usually a part of the body): මගේ පපුව රිදෙනවා. My chest hurts. මගේ ඇඟ සේරම රිදෙනවා. My whole body aches. රිදෙනවා may also mean 'to be hurt, to get hurt', but only in the sense 'to (be caused to) feel pain', not 'to be wounded or injured'. The subject will then be a noun in the dative case referring to the person who is hurt: වැටෙන්ඩ එපා! වැටුනොත් ඔය ලමයාට රි දේවී. Don't fall! If you fall, it'll hurt you. 11. යටතෙ යටතෙ is a post position with the meaning 'under, for' in the sense of 'under the jurisdiction of, subordinate to'. It requires a dependent noun or pronoun in the direct case: මම ආංඩුව යටතෙ වැඩ කරනවා. I work for the government. [page 75] ලමයා දැන් ඉන්නෙ මම යටතේ The boy is under my jurisdiction now. යටතෙ has a dative form a which is used with verbs involving a change of state, as in 'taken under (the jurisdiction of)'. ගිය අවුරුද්දෙ ලංකාවෙ ඉස්කෝල සේරම ආංඩුව යටතට ගත්තා. Last year, all schools in Ceylon were taken under the Jurisdiction of the government. 12. සම්බන්දව සම්බන්දව 'concerning, about' is a synonym for. Another synonym, which has not yet occurred, is 32 All three take a dependent noun in the direct case and may be used in the same situations: පපුවෙ අමාරු ගැන හොඳම දොස්තර තමයි ඩොකට හැන්ඩ්. පපුවෙ අමාරු සම්බන්දව හොඳම දොස්තර තමයි පපුවෙ අමාරු පිලිබඳව හොඳම දොස්තර තමයි ඩොක්ට හැන්ඩි. ඩොකට හැන්ඩි. The best doctor for chest ailments is Doctor Handy. 13. තරම් තරම් 'as much as', in addition to occurring in expressions such as ở đó 'that much may take either a dependent infinitive or a dependent noun in whatever case is required by the construction in which the phrase occurs: 32. මට වාට්ටුවකට ඇතුල්වෙන්න තරම් අසනීපයක් නෑ. No, I'm not sick enough to go into a ward. මේ පොත් සේරම කියවන්ඩ තරම් දැන් වෙලා නෑ. There isn't time to read all these books now. මහත්තයාට තරම් මට සල්ලි නෑ. I don't have as much money as the master (has). කොලඹ පලාතෙ තරම් හොඳ කෑම මේ පැත්තෙ නෑ. There isn't as much good food here as there is in the Colombo area.

[page 72] this construction generally differs in meaning from the similar one with a dependent infinitive plus තයනව (12,7) in that the construction with වනව implies that the situation involved comes about without prior arrangement, or involuntarily, while that with තයනව suggests that the situation has been prearranged or is settled: මට ඊය කලඹ ඉනඩ තඋන . i was supposed to be in colombo yesterday. මහතතය ආ නස මට ඊය කලඹ ඉනන උන . because the master came, i had to go to colombo yesterday. 5. ‘from … to …’ the english ‘from … to … ’ with time expressions is expressed in sinhalese by … ඉඳල … වන කං. the form dependent upon ඉඳල is in the genitive case as learned earlier, and the form dependent upon වන කං is in the direct case, since වන කං means literally ‘till it gets to be’. දවල දලහ ඉඳල එක වන කං from twelve noon to one. හවස පහ ඉඳල හය වන කං from five in the afternoon until six. ර දක ඉඳල එල වන කං from two a.m. (literally two at night) until dawn. the english ‘from … to …’ with place expressions is stated in sinhalese, as learned in the first lesson, by putting the place to which in the dative case: මහ ඉඳල කලතරට from here to kalutara. 6. කල some of the past tense forms of කරනව have alternate forms with a past tense stem කල- rather than කර -. there is no difference in usage or meaning. the alternate forms are: [page 73] කල = කරව (simple past) කල = කරව (emphatic past) කල = කරව (past tense verbal adjective) කලත = කරවත (conditional) 7. emphatic equational sentences when an equational sentence with an adjective as predicate attribute is transformed to the emphatic form, the assertion marker is removed from the adjective. as with other emphatic sentences, the emphasized item is frequently put last in the sentence but need not be: simple: ම පත හඳය . this book is good. emphatic: හඳ ම පත . it is this book which is good. as in other types of emphatic sentences, the emphasized form may be further emphasized by adding to it an item such as තමය or ය: simple: මහතතය ගදරට ගහන හමබවන එක වඩය හඳය . your going to (his) house and meeting (him) is better. emphatic: මහතතය ගදරට ගහන හමබවන එක තමය වඩය හඳ . it is better that you go to his house and meet him. } 8. adverbs in -0 a few adjectives in sinhalese may add to form an adverb. they must be learned as they occur. the only one that has occurred so far is a 'private'; thus a 'privately'. 2. පදගලකව වඩ කරන අයත ඉනනව. no, there are also people who work privately. 9. third person pronouns the plural of the third person pronouns ໑໖໖, ඔය අරය, එය the, she' has been given as මයල, ඔයල, අරයල, එයල 'they' (11, 3). another set of third person plural pronouns, [page 74] with no difference in meaning, may be formed by adding di-rectly to the members of the 6 set. thus: ම ගලල they (by me) මයල ඔය ගලල they (by you) = ඔයල අර ගලල they (over there) = අරයල ඒ ගලල they (in question) = එයල class 5 case endings are added to the forms. either singular or plural case forms may be used with no difference in meaning. thus: direct: ම ගලල dative: ම ගලලට, ම ගලලනට genitive: ම ගලලග, ම ගලලනග instrumental: ම ගලලගන, ම ගලලනගන 10. රදනව when the subject of 36໙໖ : 'to hurt, ache' is in the direct case, it expresses that which hurts or aches (usually a part of the body): මග පපව රදනව. my chest hurts. මග ඇඟ සරම රදනව. my whole body aches. රදනව may also mean 'to be hurt, to get hurt', but only in the sense 'to (be caused to) feel pain', not 'to be wounded or injured'. the subject will then be a noun in the dative case referring to the person who is hurt: වටනඩ එප! වටනත ඔය ලමයට ර දව. don't fall! if you fall, it'll hurt you. 11. යටත යටත is a post position with the meaning 'under, for' in the sense of 'under the jurisdiction of, subordinate to'. it requires a dependent noun or pronoun in the direct case: මම ආංඩව යටත වඩ කරනව. i work for the government. [page 75] ලමය දන ඉනන මම යටත the boy is under my jurisdiction now. යටත has a dative form a which is used with verbs involving a change of state, as in 'taken under (the jurisdiction of)'. ගය අවරදද ලංකව ඉසකල සරම ආංඩව යටතට ගතත. last year, all schools in ceylon were taken under the jurisdiction of the government. 12. සමබනදව සමබනදව 'concerning, about' is a synonym for. another synonym, which has not yet occurred, is 32 all three take a dependent noun in the direct case and may be used in the same situations: පපව අමර ගන හඳම දසතර තමය ඩකට හනඩ. පපව අමර සමබනදව හඳම දසතර තමය පපව අමර පලබඳව හඳම දසතර තමය ඩකට හනඩ. ඩකට හනඩ. the best doctor for chest ailments is doctor handy. 13. තරම තරම 'as much as', in addition to occurring in expressions such as ở đó 'that much may take either a dependent infinitive or a dependent noun in whatever case is required by the construction in which the phrase occurs: 32. මට වටටවකට ඇතලවනන තරම අසනපයක න. no, i'm not sick enough to go into a ward. ම පත සරම කයවනඩ තරම දන වල න. there isn't time to read all these books now. මහතතයට තරම මට සලල න. i don't have as much money as the master (has). කලඹ පලත තරම හඳ කම ම පතත න. there isn't as much good food here as there is in the colombo area.

Note: In some areas means simply 'curry'; not necessarily fish. සිල්ලර වෙලඳාම ' the retail trade; gen. සිල්ලර වෙලඳාමේ; µ1. සිල්ලර වෙලඳාම් Class 4 ලාබෙ 'the profit'; pl. සමාජ වැඩේ 'the social work'; pl. ຜາ ໖ Class 5 අමුත්තා 'the visitor, stranger'; pl. 4 කුස්සි අම්මා බබා 'the female cook'; indef. ໑໖໖ 4 pl. කුස්සි අම්මාලා බෑනා 'the baby, child'; pl. 'the nephew, son-in-law'; indef. 1 pl. බෑනාලා ගැනි 'the woman'; pl. වැඩකාරයා 'the servant'; pl. හෘදයා 'the fellow'; pl. [page 86] 2. NEW VERBS Class 1 බල කරනවා ලෑස්ති කරනවා සොයනවා 'force' 'make ready, prepare (or හොයනවා ) 'look for, search' Irregular හිටිනවා 'be' (animate = ໑໙ ); past ; ppl. හිටලා එක්ක එනවා 'bring (a person)'; past ໖໖ බාර දෙනවා 'hand over'; past ໖໑໒ ຫວ 3 IDIOMS නිතර 'frequently' ඉඳලා හිටලා 'now and then' බයෙන් බයෙන් 'worriedly, in fear' ඉස්පාසුවක් නෑ (with dative case subject) 'doesn't get a minute's peace' අමුතු දෙයක් 'something new' Note: 494 මදැයි දැකපු කල් ගිහින් එන්න යනවා ඇවිත් යන්න එනවා is also used with 'news': 49 σι 'Hasn't it been a long time!' 'go to visit' 'come to visit' 4. හා may The vowel in හා is pronounced with nasalization. be used like English 'oh' or ah' as an expression of surprise: හා, ගෙදර ඉන්නවා, නේද ? Ah, you are home, aren't you! is also an equivalent of English 'yes' or 'all right', in response to commands or requests, and is the common way of ans-wering them affirmatively. It is not used as an affirmative answer to questions, which are answered with without repetition of the verb (or item like with or පුලුවන් ඕන ) of [page 87] the question. Compare the following: බංඩා, මෙහ්ට එන්න. හා, මහත්තයා. Banda, come here. Yes, sir. බංද්ධා කොළඹ යනවා ද? ඔව් . මහත්තයා (යනවා). Are you going to Colombo, Banda? Yes, I am (going), sir. බංඩාට කාර් එලවන්න පුලුවන්, නේද? You can drive a car, can't you, Banda? ඔව්. මහත්තයා (පුලුවනි). Yes, sir (I can). 5. බෑ, පුලුවන් WITH PAST PARTICIPLE The form may be used with a dependent past participle either in the negative or positive form. In this construction, the negative participle plus ε means 'must' and the positive participle with @ means 'mustn't': නෞකා බෑ. කාලා බෑ. (You) must eat. (You) mustn't eat. again In questions a similar construction occurs with with the negative participle plus meaning 'must' and the positive participle plus ge meaning 'mustn't. The question form serves as an emphatic type of statement rather than a ques-tion. Compare English 'How can I drink tea?' meaning 'I certain-ly can't drink tea.' තේ බලා පුලුවන්ද? තේ නොබ පුලුවන්ද? (I) mustn't drink tea, how can I drink tea? (I) must drink tea, how can (I) not drink tea? 6. 'ILL' 'Someone is ill' may be expressed in Sinhalese in either of two ways: with the adjective qຜບ as predicate and the dative case of the person who is ill as subject, or with the instrumen-tal case of the noun අසනීපෙ as predicate and a direct case subject. There is no difference in meaning: [page 88] මහත්තයාට අසනීපයි. මහත්තයා අසනී පෙනේ. The master is sick. පොඩි හෘදයාට දැන් මාසයක් විතර අසනීපයි. පොඩ් හෘදයා දැන් මාසයක් විතර අසනීපෙන්. The little fellow has been sick for about a month now. The same can be done with the adjective ຜບ 'healthy, well' and the noun ຜບ 'good health': පුතාට දැන් සමීපයි. පුතා දැන් සමීපෙන්. (My) son is well now. 7. කම්මැලි The form කම්මැලි 'not to like, not to feel like' is used with the assertion marker in simple sentences: 7.1 When er is used with a dative subject it has the mean-ing 'not to feel like (temporarily)' or 'to be too lazy to'. It may be used with or without a dependent infinitive: මට කම්මැලියි. I don't feel like doing any-thing. මට කොහේවත් යන්න කම්මැලියි. I'm too lazy to go anywhere. 7.2 When ໑໖ is used with a subject in the direct case it means 'not to like' or 'to dislike'. In this construction it may have either a dependent infinitive or a dependent noun in the dative case as object: මහත්තයා ඒ කඩේට යන්න කම්මැලියි. The master doesn't like to go to that shop. මම නම් සමාජ වැඩවලට කම්මැලියි. As for me, I'm not interested in public service. [page 89] 7.3 As a predicate adjective, or adjective preceding a noun, කම්මැලි means 'lazy'. ඒ රස්තියාදුකාරයා බොහොම කම්මැලියි. That loafer is very lazy! අයිසෙ, තමුසෙ හරි කම්මැලි මිනිහෙක්. Friend, you are a real lazy fellow! 7.4 Note that the constructions in which those in which the opposite of occurs are like does (4, 8) and that er is in a sense : මට කොළඹ යන්ඩ ආසායි. I feel like going to Colombo. මට කොළඹ යන්ඩ කම්මැලියි. I don't feel like going to Colombo. මම කොළඹ යන්ඩ ආසායි. I like going to Colombo. මම කොළඹ යන්ඩ කම්මැලියි. I don't like going to Colombo. 8. PAST TENSE VERBAL ADJECTIVE In Lesson 28 the formation of the past tense verbal adjective was given. For example: Verb Past Tense Verbal Adjective Class 1 බලනවා බැලුව Class 2 අදිනවා φιές Class 3 තේරෙනවා තේරුන Class 1 and 3 verbal adjectives have alternate forms as follows. Class 2 verbal adjectives do not have alternate forms. Class 1. Instead of ending ina, the past tense verbal adjective may end in u oru. If the stem has two syllables and the first syllable is short as in කපනවා ending will be u. Otherwise it is u: බලනවා the [page 90] Verb බලනවා කපනවා නවත්තනවා Past Tense Verbal Adjective බැලුව කැපුව or or කැපූ නැවැත්තුව or නැවැත්තු Class 3. Instead of ending in, the verbal adjective may end in: තේරෙනවා තේරුන or තේරුනු වැටෙනවා වැටුන or වැටුනු Irregular Verbs: ending in u instead of -a. Some irregular verbs have alternate forms Those that have occurred so far are: ඉන්නවා ගන්නවා ගෙවදිනවා තියෙනවා දෙනවා or නවතිනවා පේනවා වෙනවා උන්න ගත්ත ගෙවදුන ති උන නැවතුන or පෙනුන උන or or or or or or උන්නු ගත්තු ගෙවදුනු 6 උනු නැවතුනු පෙනුනු උනු 9. PAST PARTICIPLE A past participle, when used in a subordinate clause, may have as subject either the subject of the main verb or a different subject. In the latter construction, the subject of the past participle is in the case required by the verb that is used as past participle: මහත්තයා ගිහිල්ලා මට මොකුත් කරන්න බැරි උනා. With the master gone, I couldn't do a thing. ගෙදර වැඩට උන්නු ගැනි ගිහිල්ලා දැන් ගෙදර සේරම වැඩ කරන්නෙ එයා. With the woman who did the housework gone, she does all the work in the house her-self. බංඩාට සල්ලි හම්බ වෙලා මිනි හා අද කොළඹ ගියා. Having gotten his money, Banda went to Colombo today. [page 91] 10. 'TAKE, BRING' The verbs එක්ක යනවා 'take along and ໖໖໖ ໑໙໖: 'bring along' (21, 12) are used only with a person as object, and the object is in the direct case: මම පුතා එක්ක එන්න කොළඹට යනවා. I'm going to Colombo to bring (my) son (home). සීගිරියට යන කොට නෝනා එක්ක යනවා. When I go to Sigiriya, I'm taking my wife. The verbs අරන් යනවා 'take' and අරන් එනවා bring' are used with animals or things as direct object and are alternatives to the verbs ගෙනියනවා 'take' and ගේනවා 'bring'. All of these also take objects in the direct case: මම හෙට පොතක් ගේන්නම්. මම හෙට පොතක් අරන් එන්නම්. I'll bring a book tomorrow. මම හෙට පොතක් ගෙනියන්නම්. මම හෙට පොතක් අරන් යන්නම්. I'll take a book tomorrow. 11. එක්ක The postposition đơn may be used with a noun or pronoun in the dative case meaning 'also for'. It may be used either with or without - added to the dependent noun or pronoun (compare the use of ໖໐໙ with a noun or pronoun in the direct case meaning 'with' (11, 5): මට එක්ක කෑම හදන්න. මටත් එක්ක කෑම හදන්න. Prepare food for me, too. මහත්තයා මටත් එක්ක බඩු ගත්තා ද? Did he buy goods for me, too? මම දුවටත් එක්ක ඇඳුම් ගන්න ඕන. I must buy clothes for the daughter as well. 12. The emphatic particle may be used in sentences with the negative, or with do as the negative of an imperative, equating with the English 'not at all': [page 92] මහත්තයා යන්නෙ ම නෑ. He doesn't go at all. ඔහේ යන්නම එපා. You don't go at all. උන්නැහේ වැඩක් කරන්නෙම නෑ. He doesn't do any work at all. 13. අපේ The form q6ở, which usually equates with English 'our', is sometimes used in Sinhalese where English uses 'my'. It is very common when speaking of relations or family property: අපේ පුතාට ටිකක් අසමීපයි. My son is a little sick. අපේ වත්ත දැක්කාද? Did you see my estate? 14. හිටිනවා The verb ພິທ 'to be' (animate) will replace the verb (but not ໙໙໖) in some constructions. Since the verb be used wherever may be, the student should avoid but be prepared to recognize it when it occurs: : may උන්නැහේට දුවෙක් හිටියා, නේද ? උන්නැහේට දුවෙක් උන්නා, නේද ? He had a daughter, didn't he? මේ කඩේ හිටිය ලමයා කෝ? මේ කඩේ උන්න ලමයා කෝ? Where is the boy who was in this shop? 15. SIMPLE PAST There are a small number of Class 2 verbs which, instead of forming the simple past and the past tense verbal adjective by doubling the final consonant of the stem, form it by adding -y-to the stem, with the usual vowel change where possible. Of these, two are worth nothing: Verb හිටිනවා අරිනවා 'to be' 'to open, send' Simple Past හිටියා ඇරියා Past Tense Verbal Adjective හිටිය ඇරිය [page 93] The past participles of these are like other Class 2 verbs: හිටලා, ඇරලා.

verb or a different subject. in the latter construction, the subject of the past participle is in the case required by the verb that is used as past participle: මහතතය ගහලල මට මකත කරනන බර උන. with the master gone, i couldn't do a thing. ගදර වඩට උනන ගන ගහලල දන ගදර සරම වඩ කරනන එය. with the woman who did the housework gone, she does all the work in the house her-self. බංඩට සලල හමබ වල මන හ අද කලඹ ගය. having gotten his money, banda went to colombo today. [page 91] 10. 'take, bring' the verbs එකක යනව 'take along and ໖໖໖ ໑໙໖: 'bring along' (21, 12) are used only with a person as object, and the object is in the direct case: මම පත එකක එනන කලඹට යනව. i'm going to colombo to bring (my) son (home). සගරයට යන කට නන එකක යනව. when i go to sigiriya, i'm taking my wife. the verbs අරන යනව 'take' and අරන එනව bring' are used with animals or things as direct object and are alternatives to the verbs ගනයනව 'take' and ගනව 'bring'. all of these also take objects in the direct case: මම හට පතක ගනනම. මම හට පතක අරන එනනම. i'll bring a book tomorrow. මම හට පතක ගනයනනම. මම හට පතක අරන යනනම. i'll take a book tomorrow. 11. එකක the postposition đơn may be used with a noun or pronoun in the dative case meaning 'also for'. it may be used either with or without - added to the dependent noun or pronoun (compare the use of ໖໐໙ with a noun or pronoun in the direct case meaning 'with' (11, 5): මට එකක කම හදනන. මටත එකක කම හදනන. prepare food for me, too. මහතතය මටත එකක බඩ ගතත ද? did he buy goods for me, too? මම දවටත එකක ඇඳම ගනන ඕන. i must buy clothes for the daughter as well. 12. the emphatic particle may be used in sentences with the negative, or with do as the negative of an imperative, equating with the english 'not at all': [page 92] මහතතය යනන ම න. he doesn't go at all. ඔහ යනනම එප. you don't go at all. උනනහ වඩක කරනනම න. he doesn't do any work at all. 13. අප the form q6ở, which usually equates with english 'our', is sometimes used in sinhalese where english uses 'my'. it is very common when speaking of relations or family property: අප පතට ටකක අසමපය. my son is a little sick. අප වතත දකකද? did you see my estate? 14. හටනව the verb ພິທ 'to be' (animate) will replace the verb (but not ໙໙໖) in some constructions. since the verb be used wherever may be, the student should avoid but be prepared to recognize it when it occurs: : may උනනහට දවක හටය, නද ? උනනහට දවක උනන, නද ? he had a daughter, didn't he? ම කඩ හටය ලමය ක? ම කඩ උනන ලමය ක? where is the boy who was in this shop? 15. simple past there are a small number of class 2 verbs which, instead of forming the simple past and the past tense verbal adjective by doubling the final consonant of the stem, form it by adding -y-to the stem, with the usual vowel change where possible. of these, two are worth nothing: verb හටනව අරනව 'to be' 'to open, send' simple past හටය ඇරය past tense verbal adjective හටය ඇරය [page 93] the past participles of these are like other class 2 verbs: හටල, ඇරල.

title: Lesson 31
text: Lesson 31 Lesson 31 Grammar [page101] 1. NEW NOUNS Class 1 ඇක්සිඩන්ට් එක 'accident' ටයර් එක 'tire' බ්‍රේක් එක 'brake' Class 2 ඔලුව 'the head'; gen. 26; pl. කන්ද 'the hill'; gen. ; pl. කඩුගන්නාව 'Kadugannawa'; gen. ໑໖໑໙໑໑໖ ; no pl. කොම්පැනිය 'the company'; gen.කො පැනියෙ; pl. කොම්පැනි පොලීසිය 'the police'; gen. ຜີຜ ; pl. පොලීසි වංගුව 'the curve'; gen. ; pl. o වරද 'the mistake'; gen. θόσφ; pl. ໖໒໖ වීදුරුව 'the glass'; gen. ισ; pl. θεόι හැන්දෑව 'the evening'; gen. ; අත 'the hand, arm'; gen. q; pl. 4 පරිස්සම අත has the irregular instrumental 465 Class 4 'the care, caution'; gen. ໖໖ ; no pl. කලබලේ 'haste, trouble'; pl. 2 තුවාලෙ 'wound, injury'; pl. [page 102] 2. NEW VERBS Class 1 ඉන්ගුවර් කරනවා ට කැටි කපනවා 'insure' 'discharge from hospital' 'care, caution'; gen. ; no pl. Class 2 කන්ද බහිනවා 'go down hill' Class 3 හැපෙනවා 'collide' පැලෙනවා 'get split, cracked' සීරෙනවා 'get bruised' බිඳෙනවා 'get smashed, shattered (of glass)' තැලෙනවා 'get dented' Irregular නඩු දානවා පොඩි වෙනවා 'file action' 'get smashed' 3. DATIVE CASE 3.1 අමාරු has the meaning 'difficult' when used with a subject in the direct case, but the meaning 'very 1ll' when used with a subject in the dative case: මේ පොත අමාරුයි. This book is difficult. මහත්තයාට අමාරුයි. The master is very ill. තුවාල means that someone or something is injured when the subject is in the dative case. It means that a part of something is injured with a subject in the direct case: මහත්තයාට තුවාලයි. He is injured. කාර් එකට තුවාලයි. The car is damaged. අතක් තුවාලයි. A hand (i.e., one of his hands) was injured. දොරක් තුවාලයි. A door was damaged. [page 103] 3.2 In many sentences with adjectives like the following referr-ing to health or feelings, the subject is in the dative case: මට මහන්සියි. I'm tired. මට සීතලයි. I'm cold. මට නිදිමතයි. I'm sleepy. මට බඩගිනියි. I'm hungry. මට වතුර තිබහයි. I'm thirsty. 3.3 The same construction is used with nouns like the following referring to physical conditions: මට හෙම්බිරිස්සාව. I have a cold. මට ඉසරදේ. I have a headache. මට මැලේරියාව. I have malaria. 3.4 Getting an Illness The names of illnesses (nouns) may occur with the Class 3 verb : 'get (an illness)' and a subject in the dative case. When the verb is in the simple present, the sense is future; when it is in any past tense form, the sense is past: දැන් ඇවිදින්න එපා, හෙම්බිරිස්සාව හැදෙනවා. Don't go walking now, you'll get a cold. මහත්තයාට හෙම්බිරිස්සාවක් හැදිලා. The master has caught a cold. මට ගිය සුමානෙ උන හැදුනා. Last week I got a fever. මහත්තයාට හැදුනෙ මැලේරියාව ලු. It seems that it was malaria that the master got. 3.5 'Getting Ill' The constructions in 3.1 and 3.2 with adjectives referring to bodily states or feelings and a subject in the dative case may occur with 6 in the sense of 'to get, become Here, too, the simple present implies future: මහත්තයාට හුඟක් අමාරු උනා. The master became very ill. [page 104] දැන් බර බිව්වොත් නිදිමත වෙනවා. If I drink beer now, I'll get sleepy. ලමයාට හුඟක් තුවාල වෙලා ද? Has the boy been badly injured? 3.6 'To Have an Accident' To have an accident is expressed by the verbal phrase If the subject is stated, it is in the ඇක්සිඩන්ට් වෙනවා dative case: මහත්තයාට ඇක්සිඩන්ට් එකක් උනා. හයියෙන් එලවන්න එපා; වෙනවා . ඇක්සිඩන්ට The master had an accident. Don't go fast, you'll have an accident. 4. TELLING TIME So far, a number of expressions for asking and telling time have occurred. They are summarized below and some new expressions are added: 4.1 'What time is it?' is expressed by ເປີເປີ ໖ 4? etc. (12,8). 4.11. The answer to the question 'What time is it?' is expressed as follows: 4.12 . Even hours are expressed by a numeral in the direct case with the assertion marker added: දෙකයි. two (o'clock) හතරයි. four (o'clock) දොලහයි. twelve (o'clock) 4.13 The half hours may be expressed in either one of two ways. First, it may be expressed in a manner similar to English 'one thirty', with the assertion marker added to both numerals: එකයි තිහයි. one thirty පහයි තිහයි. five thirty Second, the half hour may be expressed in a manner similar to the English 'half past one', using the form half following the numeral. The numeral is in the definite form, and a has the assertion marker added: [page 105] එක හමාරයි. half past one හය හමාරයි. half past six පහමාරයි. half past five දොලහමාරයි. half past twelve එකොලහමාරයි. half past eleven Note that in the last three examples, where the numeral ends in -ha, this ha is dropped before the ha of ໙໖໒໖. 4.14 The quarter hour may also be expressed in two ways. The first is similar to the English 'two fifteen': දෙකයි පාලහයි. two fifteen හ යයි පාලහයි. six fifteen The second way is to use the form 'quarter' following the numeral. Both the numeral and take the assertion marker: දෙකයි කාලයි. quarter past two හයයි කාලයි. quarter past six 4.15 The three-quarter hour may also be expressed in two ways. First, it may be expressed like the English 'three forty-five': තුනයි හතලිස් පහයි. three forty-five හතයි හතලිස් පහයි. seven forty-five Secondly, it may be expressed in a manner similar to the English 'quarter to seven' with the numeral in the dative case and the assertion market on කාල : එකට කාලයි. quarter to one හතට කාලයි. quarter to seven 4.16 For time after the hour, other than those mentioned above, there is only one way of stating the time. The expression used is similar to those above like 'one thirty': දෙකයි පහයි. 2:05 එකොලහයි දහයයි. 11:10 තුනයි තිස් පහයි. 3:35 [page 106] 4.17 Odd times after the half hour may be expressed in a manner similar to English 'five to six'. As with 'quarter to', the first numeral is in the dative case and the second has the assertion marker: හයට පහයි. දොලහට විසි පහයි. five (minutes) to six twenty-five (minutes) to twelve 4.2 'At what time? is expressed as follows: කීයට ද? 4.21 . In answering this question, if the time is a time to the following hour (that is, those expressions in which the first numeral is in the dative) the expression is similar to the one mentioned in the preceding section, except that the last form is in the indefinite and is followed by the word ຜາ. එකට පහක් තියා at five to one තුනට කාලක් තියා at quarter to three හතරට විසි පහක් තියා at twenty-five to four 4.22. 22. All other answers to the question 'at what time?' are similar to those mentioned in section 4.1 except that the last form is in the dative: දෙකට. එකයි තිහට. at two at 1:30 දෙකයි පහට. at 2:05 එකයි කාලට. at quarter past one තුනයි කාලට. at quarter past three එක හමාරට. at half past one at half past three තුන හමාරට. that the numeral pre-Note that it is only with the form me ceding is in the definite form without the assertion marker. 4.3. When the time is stated vaguely, as an equivalent of the English 'about', the Sinhalese expression uses a for 'about To express 'at about a time', nó is added to the expressions for 'at a time', with no other change in the expression: [page 107] එකට පහක් තියා විතර. at about five to one දෙකට විතර. at about two එකයි තිහට විතර. at about 1:30 දෙකට පහට විතර. at about 2:05 තුනයි කාලට විතර. at quarter past three එක හමාරට. at half past one To express 'It is about such and such a time (now)', ໙໒ 418 is added to the expressions for times given above. However, when nó is added the numeral preceding is in the dative case, with one exception. This exception is the situation where time to a certain hour is involved. In this case, the numeral pre-ceding a is in the indefinite: එකට විතර ඇති. It's about one. එකයි කාලට විතර ඇති. It's about quarter past one. දෙක හමාරට විතර ඇති. It's about half past two. but එකට පහක් විතර ඇති. It's about five to one. දෙකට කාලක් විතර ඇති. It's about quarter to two. The expression for 'at about what time?' is ໖໖ ປີ໙໒ ? The expression for 'about what time is it?' is ໖໖໖ ໑໙໒ φές? 5. 'MUST HAVE' 'Must have' is expressed in Sinhalese by 48 plus a dependent infinitive and a subject in the direct case: පීනසේන පනහට විතර යන්න ඇති. Jinasena must have been going about 50. ඊයෙ නම් යන්න ඇත්තේ ටිකක් කලබලෙන්. Yesterday, of course, he must have been going a little fast. 6. COMPLETELY RUINED' The expression ໑ ໑໙໖ ໑ means 'completely ruined', 'no good at all'. The item so described is usually in the genitive case, but may be in the instrumental: [page 108] කාර් එකේ නම් ගන්න දෙයක් නෑ. The car, of course, was completely ruined. මේ පොතේ ගන්න දෙයක් නෑ. මේ පොතෙන් ගන්න දෙයක් නෑ. This book is no good at all. 7. හදනවා The verb ໙໕໑໑ used with a dependent infinitive has the mean-ing 'get ready to', 'try to', 'pretend to'. The present form is likely to have the meaning 'get ready to', the past 'to try to', and the future 'to pretend to': මාත් මේ යන්නයි හදන්නේ. (Here) I am ready to go. මහත්තයා වැඩ කරන්න හැදුවා. He tried to work. මහත්තයා යන්න හදාවී. He might pretend to go. 8. ආරංචි ආරංචි, which takes the assertion marker in simple sentences, means 'hear, get to know'. It is used with a subject in the dative case and with an object that is either a noun or pronoun in the direct case or a clause with (-3) ຜາ: මට ආරංචියි වරද අනිත් මහත්තයාගෙයි කියලා. I hear that the fault was the other man's. ඒ කතාව මට ආරංචි උනා I heard that story. Note that, as in the last example, may occur with and past meaning. [page 109]

(here) i am ready to go. මහතතය වඩ කරනන හදව. he tried to work. මහතතය යනන හදව. he might pretend to go. 8. ආරංච ආරංච, which takes the assertion marker in simple sentences, means 'hear, get to know'. it is used with a subject in the dative case and with an object that is either a noun or pronoun in the direct case or a clause with (-3) ຜາ: මට ආරංචය වරද අනත මහතතයගය කයල. i hear that the fault was the other man's. ඒ කතව මට ආරංච උන i heard that story. note that, as in the last example, may occur with and past meaning. text: Lesson 32 Lesson 32 Grammar [page 115] 1. NEW NOUNS Class 2 බොරුව 'the lie'; gen. οθ ; pl. බොරු මල 'the flower'; gen. ; pl. මල් මුට්ටිය 'the pot'; gen. ; pl. මුට්ටි කෙලවර 'the end'; gen. කෙලවරේ ; pl. කෙලවරවල් Singular only: බය 'the fear'; gen. වීගමුව 'Negombo'; gen. මීගමුවේ Class 3 බේරුවල 'Beruwala'; no pl. Class 4 කඹේ 'the rope'; pl. සැරේ 'time, instance'; no pl. Class 5 සමහරු 'some people'; pl. only [page 116] Other Nouns Plural only: රා 'toddy' තෙලිජ්ජ 'sap' යුස 'Juice' පැනි 'sediment' 'syrup' මුදවාපු කිරි හකුරු 'yoghurt' 'hakuru' 2. NEW VERBS Class 1 එල්ලනවා 'hang' හැර ගහනවා තියනවා 'make a temporary ladder attached to a tree' Class 2 'put, place, leave' මදිනවා 'tap' Class 3 වෑහෙනවා 'drip' පැහෙනවා 'ferment' Irregular අමතක වෙනවා 'forget' 3. PAST PARTICIPIAL CLAUSES More than one past participial clause may occur with a single main verb. Usually a sequence of actions is involved, and commor English equivalents are such sentences as 'I go home, eat dinner and go to bed' or 'after going home and eating dinner, I'll go to bed'. මදින මිනිහා ගහට නැගලා මල අග ටිකක් කපලා මුට්ටියක් එල්ලනවා. The man who is tapping climbs the tree, cuts the flower, and hangs a pot. [page 117] මම ගෙදර ගිහිල්ලා කෑම කාලා ආපහු එන්නම්. I'll come back after going home and eating dinner. බංඩා වත්තට ගිහිල්ලා පොල් කඩලා වැටක් බැඳලා ගෙදර ගියා. Banda went to the estate, picked coconuts, built a fence, and went home. 4. NUMERAL EXPRESSIONS 4.1 සැරේ and පාර are synonyms meaning 'time, occasion, instance'. They both occur in the construction "Numeral stem plus indefinite noun" (27, 6) to express 'two times', 'three times', etc. දවසට දෙසැරයක් හැම ගහකටම නගින්න ඕන. දවසට දෙපාරක් හැම ගහකටම නගින්න ඕන. Twice a day you have to climb each tree. මේ බේත දවසට තුන් සැරයක් කෑමට පස්සේ බොන්න. මේ බේත දවසට තුන් පාරක් කෑමට පස්සේ බොන්න. Take this medicine three times a day after meals. 4.2 Although only a limited number of nouns may occur in the construction "Numeral stem plus indefinite noun," as pointed out in Lesson 27, almost all nouns can occur in a similar construc-tion with the numeral 1, the indefinite noun 3 and an indefinite noun. Note that means 'a man' and when used with 'one man': that is එක මිනිහෙක් means එක මිනිහෙක් one man එක ගහක් one tree එක පාරක් one time, one instance In emphatic sentences, when the indefinite noun with or without is emphasized, the assertion marker replaces the indefinite ending and the meaning is 'only': මට ඕන රුපියලයි. I want (only) a rupee. මට ඕන එක රුපියලයි. I want only one rupee. [page 118] 5. 'SIMILAR TO' සමාන is used as a postposition with a dependent noun in the dative case meaning 'similar to, like'. The phrases formed in this way act as adjectives: රා බරවලට සමානයි. Toddy is similar to beer. මේ ‍නෝනා අපේ අම්මාට සමානයි. This woman is like my mother. අරකට සමාන පොතක් ඕන. I want a book similar to that one. මට අපේ මාමාට සමාන මහත්තයෙක් හම්බ උනා. I met a gentleman like my uncle. එක The phrase 'alike'. like ໖໖ ໑໖ means the same as 'identical, Both phrases may act as adjectives: මේ ලමයි දෙන්නා එක සමානයි. මේ ලමයි දෙන්නා එක වගෙයි. These two boys are alike. ඇමෙරිකාවෙ මිනිස්සුයි ඉංගිරිසි මිනිස්සුයි එක සමානයි. ඇමෙරිකාවෙ මිනිස්සුයි ඉංගිරිසි මිනිස්සුයි එක වගෙයි. Americans and Englishmen are alike. However, only a not ໖໖ ຜາ may be used with a verb: මේ පොත් දෙක මට පේන්නෙ එක වගෙයි. These two books look alike to me. මේ ලමයි දෙන්නාට එක වගේ වැඩ කරන්න බෑ These two boys can't work alike. 6. 8, 2 When 'this' and 'that' occur before the postposition ලඟ 'near', they take the forms and respectively. These phrases have the meaning 'next to this', 'next to that': මී ලග සුමානෙ මට පවුල බලන්න යන්නම්. Next week I'm going to see my family. මී ලග හෝටලේට යන්න. Go to the hotel next to this one. [page 119] වාමාගෙ කඩේට යන්න එපා. ඊ ලඟ කඩේට යන්න. Don't go to (your) uncle's shop. Go to the one next to it. In the dative case, these expressions are used as adverbs meaning 'next' (after this, after that). ඊ ලඟට මම ගෙදර ගියා. Next (after that) I went home. ට ලඟට පස්වෙනි පාඬම කියවමු. Next (after this) let's read the fifth lesson. 7. 'GET A CHANCE TO හම්බ වෙනවා 'meet', with a dependent infinitive and a subject in the dative case, has the usual English equivalent 'get a chance to', 'have the opportunity to': මට මේ සුමානෙ කොහේවත් යන්න හම්බ වෙන්නෙ නෑ. This week I won't get a chance to go anywhere. ඔහේට පැනි කන්න හම්බ උනා, නේ? You have had a chance to eat treacle, haven't you? 8. 'CLIMB, DESCEND' නගිනවා 'climb up', 'ascend', and ໑໙: 'climb down', 'descend' frequently imply a point to which or from which and hence usually occur with a noun or pronoun in either the dative or instrumental case: ඔහේ ගහෙන් බහින්න.You come down from the tree! ඔහේ මෙතෙන්ට බහින්න.Come down here! ඔහේ බස් එකට නගින්න.You get into the bus. මෙතනින් නගින්න පටන්ගන්න.Begin climbing from here. 9. බලනවා බලනවා 'to see may have as object a clause with the verb in the simple form: [page 120] මම බංඩා වැටක් බඳිනවා බැලුවා. I saw Banda build a fence. එතකොට හකුරු හදනවාත් බලන්න පුලුවනි. Then you can watch them make hakuru, too. 10. 'SEE' The present tense simple and emphatic forms of the verb ເລິຫາ 'to see are used only in a few fixed idiomatic expressions. Instead, Sinhalese uses the verb as to express 'to see' in the present tense. In forms other than the present simple and present emphatic, either ເລິຫາ or පේනවා may be used with no difference in meaning. Note that ໑໙໖ always takes a dative case and ລິຫາ a direct case subject; but either verb may take a direct case noun or pronoun or a simple verb clause as object: මට මිනිහෙක් එනවා පේනවා. I see a man coming. ඔහේට පේන්නෙ කොයි පන්සල ද? Which temple do you see? මම හකුරු හදනවා දැක්කා. මට හකුරු හදනවා පෙනුනා. I saw hakuru being made. 11. 'FALSE' The noun ລາ means 'the lie'. However, Sinhalese commonly uses the plural in situations where English would use the adjective 'false', as in the idiom 4, ເລ 4? 'true or false?'; literally 'the truth or lies?': ඒ කතාව බොරු. That story is false. ඒක බොරු කතාවක්. That is a false story.

[page 118] 5. 'similar to' සමන is used as a postposition with a dependent noun in the dative case meaning 'similar to, like'. the phrases formed in this way act as adjectives: ර බරවලට සමනය. toddy is similar to beer. ම ‍නන අප අමමට සමනය. this woman is like my mother. අරකට සමන පතක ඕන. i want a book similar to that one. මට අප මමට සමන මහතතයක හමබ උන. i met a gentleman like my uncle. එක the phrase 'alike'. like ໖໖ ໑໖ means the same as 'identical, both phrases may act as adjectives: ම ලමය දනන එක සමනය. ම ලමය දනන එක වගය. these two boys are alike. ඇමරකව මනසසය ඉංගරස මනසසය එක සමනය. ඇමරකව මනසසය ඉංගරස මනසසය එක වගය. americans and englishmen are alike. however, only a not ໖໖ ຜາ may be used with a verb: ම පත දක මට පනන එක වගය. these two books look alike to me. ම ලමය දනනට එක වග වඩ කරනන බ these two boys can't work alike. 6. 8, 2 when 'this' and 'that' occur before the postposition ලඟ 'near', they take the forms and respectively. these phrases have the meaning 'next to this', 'next to that': ම ලග සමන මට පවල බලනන යනනම. next week i'm going to see my family. ම ලග හටලට යනන. go to the hotel next to this one. text: Lesson 33 Lesson 33 Grammar [page 131] 1. NEW NOUNS Class 2 අයිතිවාසිකම right; gen. 4າຜິ pl. අයිතිවාසිකම් කැමැත්ත wish; gen. pl. කැමති ගනන number; gen. pl. ගනන් සැනේට් සබාව the Senate; gen. සැනේට් සබාවෙ pl. සැනේට් සබා සුලු ජාතිය minority community; gen. ຜາຜ pl. සුලුජාති Class 4 කොට්ටාසෙ district, constituency; pl. ພວມຜ party; pl. ໖໖ Class 5 අගමැතිතුමා Prime Minister; pl. අගමැතිතුමාලා, අගමැතිවරු අග්‍රාණ්ඩුකාරතුමා Governor General; pl. අගාංඩුකාරතුමාලා ඇමතිවරයා Minister; pl. φιλόι නායකයා leader; pl. නායකයො නියෝජිතයා representative; pl. ປີຜ මන්ත්‍රීවරයා member (of Parliament); pl. මහ රැජින Queen; pl. මහ රැජිනියො උපදෙස් advice (plural only) [page 132] 2. NEW VERBS Class 1 අදහස් කරනවා intend තෝරනවා select පත්කරනවා appoint පවත්තනවා hold, conduct විවුර්ත කරනවා declare open 3. THE OBJECT MARKER -อ The direct object of a verb in Colloquial Sinhalese is gener-ally in the direct case. However, if the direct object is an animate noun or pronoun, some speakers may mark it by adding a form -0. In the singular, -0 is added to the direct case form, and in the plural it is usually added to the stem with that precedes case endings. Singular Object හරකාව ගුරුවරයාව man one head of cattle teacher Plural Object මිනිස්සුන්ව හරකුන්ව ගුරුවරුන්ව When is added to the first person pronouns and අපි, the results are මාව and අපව. Some speakers use more frequently than others. It is always an alternate for the direct case form, but only in the direct object position, and only with animate forms: මම මිනිහාව දැක්කා. I saw the fellow. මීනි හා මාව දැක්කා. The fellow saw me. 4. 'TWO OR THREE' In Lesson 21 expressions for 'two or three, 'three or four,' etc., were introduced. These were formed with both numerals in the indefinite form and could be made with either inanimate or animate numerals: [page 133] එකක් දෙකක් එ ක්කෙනෙක් දෙන්නෙක් For these expressions there are alternatives which occur for certain numerals as follows: 1. For inanimate numerals there is an alternative with the first numeral in the definite form and the second numeral either definite or indefinite depending on sense. for the most part limited to the following This alternative is numeral combinations: දෙක තුන two or three දෙක තුනක් (a) two or three තුන හතර three or four තුන හතරක් (a) three or four හත අට seven or eight හත අටක් (a) seven or eight මේ පොත් තුන හතර කඩේ තියන්න. Put these three or four books in the shop. මට සිගරැට් තුන හතරක් ගන්න ඕන. I want to get three or four cigarettes. 2. For animate numerals there is an alternative with the first numeral in the stem form and the second numeral either definite or indefinite depending on sense. This alternative is largely limited to the following combinations: දෙතුන් දෙනා two or three දෙතුන් දෙනෙක් (a) two or three තුන් හතර දෙනා three or four තුන් හතර දෙනෙක් (a) three or four හතර පස් දෙනා four or five හතර පස් දෙනෙක් (4) four or five හත් අට දෙනා seven or eight හත් අට දෙනෙක් (a) seven or eight දහ දොලොස් දෙනා ten or twelve දහ දොලොස් දෙනෙක් (a) ten or twelve වස තිස් දෙනා twenty or thirty විසි තිස් දෙනෙක් (a) twenty or thirty මේ ලමයි දෙතුන් දෙනාට වඩුවැඩ උගන්නන්න. Teach these two or three boys carpentry. මිනිස්සු දෙතුන් දෙනෙකුට වැඩියෙ යවන්න එපා. Don't send more than two or three men. [page 134] 5. OTHER In positive statements the form a when used with a singular indefinite noun, equates with English 'another (an additional one) and equates with English 'another (a different one)'. These forms may be used with plural nouns with the same distinc-tion in meaning; that is 'other (additional)' and 'other (different)'. මට තව පොතක් දෙන්න. Give me another book (This one isn't enough). මෙහෙ තව පොත් තියෙනවා ද? Are there other (i.e., more) books here? මට වෙන පොතක් දෙන්න. Give me another book (I don't like this one). මෙහෙ වෙන පොත් තියෙනවාද? Are there other books here? (These won't do.) In negative sentences only a is used, and it may have either meaning: මට වෙන පොතක් එපා. I don't want another book (either one more or one instead of this one!). මෙහෙ වෙන පොත් නැද්ද? Aren't there other books here? (Either any more or others to replace these.) The form 438 equates with the English 'the other' either singular or plural: මට අනිත් පොත දෙන්න. Give me the other book. අනිත් බඩු ගෙනාවෙ නැද්ද? Didn't you bring the other goods? [page 135] The emphatic particle when added to se 'other' produces an adverbial expression equating with English 'separately': මම වෙනම වැඩ කරන්නම්. I'll work separately. ඒ මිනිස්සුන්ට වෙනට ආසනයක් නෑ. Those people don't have a separate representative (lit. They don't have a seat separately). 6. COMPARATIVE DEGREE It has already been noted that there is a comparative construc-tion with the form ໖ plus a dependent noun in the dative case: මේ පොත අරකට වැඩියෙ හොඳයි. This book is better than that one. For many adjectives the ໖ in meaning. Thus: may be omitted with no change The student should note these when he meets them. මේ පොත අරකට වැඩියෙ ලොකුයි. or මේ පොත අරකට ලොකුයි. This book is bigger than that one. මේ පොත අරකට වැඩියෙ පොඩියි. or මේ පොත අරකට පොඩියි. This book is smaller than that one. Other examples are: කොට්ටාස ගාන ඊට අඩුයි. The number of districts is smaller than that. මගේ චන්ද ගාන ඊට වැඩියි. The number of votes I got is greater than that. 7. 'EXCEPT' The form reóa 'except,' 'with the exception of, 'besides,' is used with a dependent noun, the case of which depends on the construction: [page 136] මහත්තයා ඇරෙන්න තව හය දෙනෙක් ඉන්නවා. There are six besides the master. මට ඇරෙන්න වෙන කාටවත් සිංහල බෑ. No one knows Sinhalese except me. 8. REFLEXIVE PRONOUN The reflexive pronoun in Sinhalese is ໑໖ (with an alternate form ). It is usually used in the third person; 'he him-self, 'they themselves, etc. It is occasionally used in the first or second person, but the student should avoid this, since 1t is so used only in special circumstances. තමන් (තමුන් ) has the usual case forms: DIRECT තමන් (or තමුන් ) DATIVE තමන්ට (or තමුන්ට ) GENITIVE තමන්ගෙ (or තමුන්ගෙ ) INSTRUMENTAL තමන්ගෙන් (or තමුන්ගෙන්) It may be used as a pronoun referring to the same person as the subject, but it is not obligatory: ඒ මිනිස්සු එයාලාගෙ කාර්වලින් යාවී. ඒ මිනිස්සු තමන්ගෙ (තමුන්ගේ) කා වලින් යාවී. Those men will go in their (own) cars. ඔය ලමයි ඔය ලමයින්ට ඕන පොත් අර සාප්පුවෙන් ගන්න. ඔය ලමයි තමන්ට (තමුන්ට ) ඕන පොත් අර සාප්පුවෙන් ගන්න. You (boys) get the books you want from that shop. 9. වෙනුවෙන් The form G is used with a dependent noun in the direct case and means 'for, on behalf of. The form G໖໖໖ is also used with a dependent noun in the direct case and means 'for, in place of.' මම මහත්තයා වෙනුවෙන් රැස්වීමට යනවා. I will go to the meeting for the master. [page 137] අම්මා සල්ලි වෙනුවට පොල් දුන්නා. Mother gave coconuts in place of money. 10. 'WHAT FOR' The form 50 means 'what for?,' 'for what purpose?' මම ඒ පල් කතාව අහන්නෙ මොකට ද? What should I listen to that dry talk for? 11. අය අය 'they,' 'those people' is used only with some preceding form qualifying it: මේ අය these people වැඩ කරන අය working people හුඟක් අය many people 12. 'INTEND' The verb ໕໕໙໖໑໙: 'intend to takes a subject in the direct case and a dependent infinitive. ඒ අය සිංහල ඉගනගන්න අදහස් කරනවා. Those people intend to learn Sinhalese. මම ලබන සුමානෙ මේක ඉවර කරන්න අදහස් කරනවා. I intend to finish this one next week. 13. 'ALL' The form ඔක්කොම සේරම native for 'all,' 'everybody' may be used as an alter-Like සේරම, ඔක්කොම may go either before or after the plural noun that it qualifies: මේ ඔක්කොට පොත් අලුත්. මේ සේරම පොත් අලුත්. All of these books are new. [page 138] මට මේ පොත් ඔක්කොම ඕන උනා. මට මේ පොත් සේරම ඕන උනා. I needed all of these books. 14. TERMS OF RESPECT To form terms of respect for people in high ranking positions, the forms වරයා or තුමා are added to noun stems. The plurals are වරු and තුමාලා : ඇමතිතුමා ඇමතිතුමාලා or ඇමතිවරයා ඇමතිවරු the minister the ministers ඇමතිතුමාලාත් රැස්වීමට එනවා ද? or ඇමතිවරුත් රැස්වීමට එනවාද? Are the ministers coming to the meeting, too? 15. ADJECTIVES Adjectives may have an indefinite form. This form, like the indefinite of nouns, shows certain stem variations: Adjective නරක නියම fixed ලොකු පොඩ් small අලුත් කැමති good bad big new like Indefinite Form හොඳ හොඳක් නරකක් නියමයක් ලොකුවක් පොඩියක් අලුතක් කැමැත්තක් The indefinite form is used in negative construction like the following, implying 'not particularly.' ඒක හොඳක් නෑ. That isn't very good. ඒ ගාන නියමයක් නෑ. That number isn't particularly fixed. [page 139]

'two or three' in lesson 21 expressions for 'two or three, 'three or four,' etc., were introduced. these were formed with both numerals in the indefinite form and could be made with either inanimate or animate numerals: [page 133] එකක දකක එ කකනක දනනක for these expressions there are alternatives which occur for certain numerals as follows: 1. for inanimate numerals there is an alternative with the first numeral in the definite form and the second numeral either definite or indefinite depending on sense. for the most part limited to the following this alternative is numeral combinations: දක තන two or three දක තනක (a) two or three තන හතර three or four තන හතරක (a) three or four හත අට seven or eight හත අටක (a) seven or eight ම පත තන හතර කඩ තයනන. put these three or four books in the shop. මට සගරට තන හතරක ගනන ඕන. i want to get three or four cigarettes. 2. for animate numerals there is an alternative with the first numeral in the stem form and the second numeral either definite or indefinite depending on sense. this alternative is largely limited to the following combinations: දතන දන two or three දතන දනක (a) two or three තන හතර දන three or four තන හතර දනක (a) three or four හතර පස දන four or five හතර පස දනක (4) four or five හත අට දන seven or eight හත අට දනක (a) seven or eight දහ දලස දන ten or twelve දහ දලස දනක (a) ten or twelve වස තස දන twenty or thirty වස තස දනක (a) twenty or thirty ම ලමය දතන දනට වඩවඩ උගනනනන. teach these two or three boys carpentry. මනසස දතන දනකට වඩය යවනන එප. don't send more than two or three men. [page 134] 5. other in positive statements the form a when used with a singular indefinite noun, equates with english 'another (an additional one) and equates with english 'another (a different one)'. these forms may be used with plural nouns with the same distinc-tion in meaning; that is 'other (additional)' and 'other (different)'. මට තව පතක දනන. give me another book (this one isn't enough). මහ තව පත තයනව ද? are there other (i.e., more) books here? මට වන පතක දනන. give me another book (i don't like this one). මහ වන පත තයනවද? are there other books here? (these won't do.) in negative sentences only a is used, and it may have either meaning: මට වන පතක එප. i don't want another book (either one more or one instead of this one!). මහ වන පත නදද? aren't there other books here? (either any more or others to replace these.) the form 438 equates with the english 'the other' either singular or plural: මට අනත පත දනන. give me the other book. අනත බඩ ගනව නදද? didn't you bring the other goods? [page 135] the emphatic particle when added to se 'other' produces an adverbial expression equating with english 'separately': මම වනම වඩ කරනනම. i'll work separately. ඒ මනසසනට වනට ආසනයක න. those people don't have a separate representative (lit. they don't have a seat separately). 6. comparative degree it has already been noted that there is a comparative construc-tion with the form ໖ plus a dependent noun in the dative case: ම පත අරකට වඩය හඳය. this book is better than that one. for many adjectives the ໖ in meaning. thus: may be omitted with no change the student should note these when he meets them. ම පත අරකට වඩය ලකය. or ම පත අරකට ලකය. this book is bigger than that one. ම පත අරකට වඩය පඩය. or ම පත අරකට පඩය. this book is smaller than that one. other examples are: කටටස ගන ඊට අඩය. the number of districts is smaller than that. මග චනද ගන ඊට වඩය. the number of votes i got is greater than that. 7. 'except' the form reóa 'except,' 'with the exception of, 'besides,' is used with a dependent noun, the case of which depends on the construction: [page 136] මහතතය ඇරනන තව හය දනක ඉනනව. there are six besides the master. මට ඇරනන වන කටවත සංහල බ. no one knows sinhalese except me. 8. reflexive pronoun the reflexive pronoun in sinhalese is ໑໖ (with an alternate form ). it is usually used in the third person; 'he him-self, 'they themselves, etc. it is occasionally used in the first or second person, but the student should avoid this, since 1t is so used only in special circumstances. තමන (තමන ) has the usual case forms: direct තමන (or තමන ) dative තමනට (or තමනට ) genitive තමනග (or තමනග ) instrumental තමනගන (or තමනගන) it may be used as a pronoun referring to the same person as the subject, but it is not obligatory: ඒ මනසස එයලග කරවලන යව. ඒ මනසස තමනග (තමනග) ක වලන යව. those men will go in their (own) cars. ඔය ලමය ඔය ලමයනට ඕන පත අර සපපවන ගනන. ඔය ලමය තමනට (තමනට ) ඕන පත අර සපපවන ගනන. you (boys) get the books you want from that shop. 9. වනවන the form g is used with a dependent noun in the direct case and means 'for, on behalf of. the form g໖໖໖ is also used with a dependent noun in the direct case and means 'for, in place of.' මම මහතතය වනවන රසවමට යනව. i will go to the meeting for the master. [page 137] අමම සලල වනවට පල දනන. mother gave coconuts in place of money. 10. 'what for' the form 50 means 'what for?,' 'for what purpose?' මම ඒ පල කතව අහනන මකට ද? what should i listen to that dry talk for? 11. අය අය 'they,' 'those people' is used only with some preceding form qualifying it: ම අය these people වඩ කරන අය working people හඟක අය many people 12. 'intend' the verb ໕໕໙໖໑໙: 'intend to takes a subject in the direct case and a dependent infinitive. ඒ අය සංහල ඉගනගනන අදහස කරනව. those people intend to learn sinhalese. මම ලබන සමන මක ඉවර කරනන අදහස කරනව. i intend to finish this one next week. 13. 'all' the form ඔකකම සරම native for 'all,' 'everybody' may be used as an alter-like සරම, ඔකකම may go either before or after the plural noun that it qualifies: ම ඔකකට පත අලත. ම සරම පත අලත. all of these books are new. [page 138] මට ම පත ඔකකම ඕන උන. මට ම පත සරම ඕන උන. i needed all of these books. 14. terms of respect to form terms of respect for people in high ranking positions, the forms වරය or තම are added to noun stems. the plurals are වර and තමල : ඇමතතම ඇමතතමල or ඇමතවරය ඇමතවර the minister the ministers ඇමතතමලත රසවමට එනව ද? or ඇමතවරත රසවමට එනවද? are the ministers coming to the meeting, too? 15. adjectives adjectives may have an indefinite form. this form, like the indefinite of nouns, shows certain stem variations: adjective නරක නයම fixed ලක පඩ small අලත කමත good bad big new like indefinite form හඳ හඳක නරකක නයමයක ලකවක පඩයක අලතක කමතතක the indefinite form is used in negative construction like the following, implying 'not particularly.' ඒක හඳක න. that isn't very good. ඒ ගන නයමයක න. that number isn't particularly fixed. [page 139]

title: Lesson 34
text: Lesson 34 Lesson 34 Grammar [page 146] 1. NEW NOUNS Class 1 කූල්ඩ්‍රින්ක් එක the cool drink; pl. කුල්ල්ඩ්‍රින් කන්ක්ස් පික්චර් එක the picture, movie වෙම්බ්ලි එක the Wembley ෂෝ එක the show f පිල්ම් එක the film හෝල් එක the hall Class 2 අව්ව the sunshine; gen. ආසාව the desire; gen. ; no pl. ගින්දර the fire; gen. ; p1. ආසාවල් ගාල්ල Galle; gen. ; no pl. ; no pl. චිත්‍ර පටය the movie; gen. ບຜ ; p1. චිත්‍රපට හිත the mind; gen. ; p1. හිත් සින්දුව the song; gen. ; p1. සින්දු Class 4 දේසගුනේ the climate; no pl. රස්නේ the heat; no pl. Other Nouns: හින්දි Hindi; no pl. 2. NEW VERBS අල්ලනවා ඉක්මන් කරනවා catch, appeal to දැනෙනවා hurry feel, perceive නතර වෙනවා stop, tarry පායනවා clear up, become dry and hot පෙන්නනවා show බහිනවා go down, descend [page 147] 3. THE PAST CONCESSIVE FORM Sinhalese has a past concessive form of the verb made by drop-ping the final, from the past tense form of the verb and adding -: Verb Simple Past Past Concessive කපනවා cut කැපුවා කැපුවත් කරනවා do, make කෙරුවා කෙරුවත් වෙනවා be, become උනා උනත් ඉන්නවා be උන්නා උන්නත් B යෙනවා be ති උනා තිඋනත් බදිනවා fry බැද්දා බැද්දත් වැටෙනවා fall වැටුනා වැටුනත් The concessive form is used to form clauses which are equiva-lent tomose in English introduced by 'even if,' 'even though': මහත්තයා ගියත් මට යන්න විදියක් නෑ. Even if the master goes, I have no way of going. ටැක්සියකින් ගියත් පරක්කු වේවී. Even if he goes by taxi he'll be late. මේ මස් බැද්දත් රස නෑ. Even if this meat is fried it is not tasty. A negative concessive clause may be formed by adding - before the concessive verb: ඔහේ නොගියත් මම යනවා. Even if you don't go, I'll go. වැඩ නොකෙරුවත් සල්ලි හම්බවෙනවා. Even if I don't work, I'll get money. 4. TO BEGIN' Besides using පටන් ගන්නවා with a dependent Infinitive in the meaning 'to begin' (Lesson 10), the verb as may be used by itself with the same meaning. The verb when used by itself in [page 148] this construction is likely to imply a certain amount of disapproval or dislike for the action involved: වහින්න ගත්තාම දිගටම වහිනවා. When it starts raining, it keeps right on. මන් හා එහෙම කතා කරන්න ගත්තාම, කවුරුවත් කට අරින්නෙ නෑ. When he begins to talk like that, no one else opens his mouth. 5. 'INSIDE' AND 'OUTSIDE' The form e 'inside, a noun of Class 2, functions as a post-position with a dependent noun in the direct case. Since it is a noun, the form 4e will appear in whatever case is required by the construction in which it appears: ගේ ඇතුලට යන්න! Go inside the house! එයා හොල් එක ඇතුලෙන් පොත් වගයක් ගෙනාවා. He brought some books out of the hall. The form 80 'outside,' a noun of Class 3, also functions as a postposition. Like 44, 80 will appear in the case required by the construction in which it appears. A noun dependent on 30 is in the instrumental case unless 80 itself is in the instrumental case, in which event the dependent noun will be in the dative case: හෝල් එකෙන් පිට ඒ මිනිස්සු හූ කිව්වා. Those people hooted outside the hall. වත්තට පිටින් ඒ ගොල්ල පාරක් හැදුවා. Those people built a road along the outside of the estate. Note that the expressions 'to look inside' or 'to look outside! require and 80 to be in the genitive case: හෝල් එක ඇතුලෙ බලන්න. Look inside the hall. [page 149] මම ගෙයින් පිට බැලුවා. I looked outside the house. 6. 'HALF' With expressions of quantity, but not numerals, the form means 'half. The noun dependent on is in the plural form: f පිල්ම් එකට තියෙන්නෙ තව පැය බාගයයි. There is still a half hour before the film starts. මේ වැඩ කරන්න තව දවස් බාගයක් ඕන. We still need a half day to finish this work. 7. 'TO FEEL' The verb a 'feel' takes a subject in the dative case and an object in the direct case. In many instances in which English uses an adjective with the verb 'feel, Sinhalese uses a noun: මට අද රස්නෙන්නෙ දැනෙනවා. I feel the heat today. 8. හින්දා හින්දා 'because, since' in 'because, since' may replace ທິຜ any construction in which the latter occurs (15,6). අව්ව සැර හින්දා අපි චිත්‍රපටියක් බලන්න යමු. අව්ව සැර නිසා අපි චිත්‍රපටයක් බලන්න යමු. Since the sun is so hot, let's go see a movie. පෙරේරා යාපනේට ගිය හින්දා මම කාර් එක මෙහෙට ගෙනාවා. පෙරේරා යාපනේට ගිය නිසා මම කාර් එක මෙහෙට ගෙනාවා. Because Perera went to Jaffna, I brought the car here. වත්තෙ වැඩ නැති හින්දා මම ගමට ආවා. වත්තෙ වැඩ නැති නිසා මම ගමට ආවා. Since there is no work in the estate, I came home. [page 150] 9. THE 3 FORM The form of the verb (Lesson 10) has an alternate form which may be used in place of it with no difference in meaning. title: Getting Started
text: # Getting Started ## Who is this dictionary for? This dictionary is primarily intended for people trying to decode and produce Sinhala at all registers. That means people are learning Sinhala as a second or heritage language and hope to be able to speak and or read at all registers. ## What this means in practice All of the existing dictionaries are oriented towards people who can already speak Sinhala and need to produce or decode English. As such, they will not include things such as verbal tenses, noun plurals, pronoun variations, register, etc. Therefore these are the very things that must be included in the SELD.
